articles.title: Hasan Piker is becoming the 'face of the progressive movement,' former Democratic operative warns
articles.excerpt:
Evan Barker says campaigning with the controversial Twitch streamer may mobilize progressive voters but risks hurting candidates in competitive states.

Controversial Twitch streamer Hasan Piker has f...
articles.body_text:
Evan Barker says campaigning with the controversial Twitch streamer may mobilize progressive voters but risks hurting candidates in competitive states.

Controversial Twitch streamer Hasan Piker has found himself at the center of a debate about the direction of the Democratic Party and generations of voters to come. However, recently on his stream, which he does for hours every day, the far-left commentator has claimed the media is making him out to have more influence than he actually does.

Evan Barker, author of "Nothing Left: Confessions Of A Democratic Operative," disagrees with Piker's analysis of his own popularity — he has more than 3 million followers on Twitch and millions more across other social media accounts — pointing to the increasing number of candidates who have invited him to campaign with them.

"Why would these candidates have this desire to bring him into their state, to campaign alongside him if he wasn't influential, to hold press junkets with him, to invite him to barbecues? Like, why would they be doing that if he didn't have influence? Like, clearly, he does," Barker told Fox News Digital.

Barker is no stranger to Democratic politics. She raised tens of millions of dollars for Democratic candidates, campaigned for Hillary Clinton and worked for candidates backed by Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt., and Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-N.Y.

EX-DEM OPERATIVE DETAILS 'NEW DONOR ESTABLISHMENT' BEHIND MAMDANI-ERA PROGRESSIVES: 'NOT FROM THE GRASSROOTS'

Former Democrat operative Evan Barker says the party needs to realize that controversial Twitch streamer Hasan Piker is quickly becoming the face of their movement. (Julia Demaree Nikhinson/AP Photo)

Barker eventually broke with the party in 2024, a journey she details in her new book. She told Fox News Digital that Democrats are "testing their limits with the popularity" in areas of the country that aren't deep blue, especially when campaigning with Piker.

"It's one thing to appear on somebody's podcast, it's another to have them come campaign for you," she said.

Piker's hours-long stream primarily focuses on politics. He has backed several candidates in the 2026 cycle, including Michigan Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed and Wisconsin gubernatorial candidate Francesca Hong.

While El-Sayed won his primary race, Hong lost to Milwaukee County Executive David Crowley, who has since said he was not planning on campaigning with Piker.

Piker's long history of incendiary and far-left rhetoric has made him an easy target for Republicans. From his retracted comments about saying the U.S. "deserved" 9/11, to his praise of Chinese dictator Mao Zedong, and the hours of talking he does every day, there's no shortage of comments for which Piker and his allies could be held to account.

When asked what she would tell candidates who are thinking about campaigning with the Twitch streamer, Barker told Fox News Digital that she would advise against it.

"I would say that the juice isn't worth the squeeze," she said. "Yeah, you're trying to appeal to younger voters, you're trying to drive out your base, but how do you win a general election aligning with him?"

Former Democrat operative Evan Barker says she would advise candidates to not campaign with Hasan Piker. (Julia Demaree Nikhinson/AP Photo)

DEMOCRAT ESTABLISHMENT STRIKES BACK AS SOCIALIST CANDIDATE DOWNED IN BATTLEGROUND PRIMARY

While Barker has expressed skepticism about Piker, she said she often hears those on the left defend their relationship with the streamer by comparing him to another media personality: Joe Rogan.

During the 2024 campaign cycle, then-Vice President Kamala Harris was criticized for not appearing on Rogan's show while running for president, particularly after both now-Vice President JD Vance and now-President Donald Trump sat for interviews with him. Some have made the case that Piker could serve as an alternative to Rogan, but Barker disagrees.

"Hasan Piker is not at all like Joe Rogan, actually. So, the charm of Joe Rogan, what makes his show so powerful is that he talks about politics sometimes. Politics is sometimes peppered into his conversations, but by and large, the majority of the time, he's not talking about politics," she said. "Whereas Hasan Piker, that's pretty much all he talks about."

She also noted that some of Piker's rhetoric that appeals to younger voters might not resonate with larger populations in parts of the country that are not deep blue.

"At the end of the day, I would remind these progressive candidates, it's not just about pleasing your staff, it's not just about pleasing, you know, the young people that are in this movement. If you want to win places like Wisconsin, if you want to win places like Michigan, you have to be patriotic," she said. "The Rust Belt is filled with hardworking patriotic Americans who don't feel the way that Hasan Piker does."

Hasan Piker has backed several candidates, including Francesca Hong, who lost Wisconsin's Democratic gubernatorial primary in August 2026. (Joshua Lott/Getty Images)

WISCONSIN DEMOCRATIC VOTERS CHALK SOCIALIST FRANCESCA HONG'S STUNNING LOSS UP TO ELECTABILITY CONCERNS

As Democrats weigh the consequences of backlash for campaigning with Piker against the access to younger voters that he brings, Barker says the streamer is quickly becoming well known offline as well. She argued that Piker is "probably the biggest podcaster, live streamer" that the Democrats have at their disposal.

"He's quickly becoming a household name. He's quickly becoming the face of the progressive movement," she said.

Barker acknowledged that some progressives may not be "comfortable" with Piker as a de facto leader, calling his rise a "monster that they've created themselves." She also compared the current moment to previous shifts within the progressive movement, arguing that figures and ideas once embraced by the left are later dismissed as excesses of an earlier era.

Twitch streamer Hasan Piker appeared on the campaign trail with Michigan Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed. (Julia Demaree Nikhinson/AP Photo)

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

Barker pointed specifically to recent discussions of "Woke 1" after Ocasio-Cortez's invocation of the term last week, arguing that Democrats have yet to reckon with the consequences of that period around 2020, which was marked by a surge in racial identity politics and progressive groupthink.

"People's lives were ruined because of 'woke 1.' It wasn't just some mass delusion or mass hysteria that we all went through... It pushed people away from Democratic politics," she said.

Barker argued that Democrats' continued willingness to align with figures like Piker shows the party has yet to move beyond that period.

"I think that there needs to be a true reckoning in the progressive movement and in the Democratic Party for people to really be able to heal and move on from this," she said.

Fox News Digital reached out to Piker for comment.

Rachel Wolf is a media and culture reporter for Fox News Digital.

articles.title: Who will be the next White House press secretary?
articles.excerpt:
Karoline Leavitt’s abrupt departure has sparked a tough race inside Trump’s circle for the prominent position

Karoline Leavitt’s surprise resignation as the White House press secretary is set to trig...
articles.body_text:
Karoline Leavitt’s abrupt departure has sparked a tough race inside Trump’s circle for the prominent position

Karoline Leavitt’s surprise resignation as the White House press secretary is set to trigger a sharp-elbowed race inside Donald Trump’s world for one of the most prominent positions in the Trump administration.

Several names have circulated since the US president announced that Leavitt would step down at the end of the month to spend more time with her family.

Here are some of the possible contenders.

Cheung currently serves as the White House communications director, and has worked closely with Leavitt throughout the second Trump administration. When he praised the outgoing press secretary for her tenure on Wednesday, Leavitt joked on social media that the pair had survived “many, many news cycles” together.

Habba is a loyal ally of the president who served as his personal lawyer before becoming a short-lived US attorney for New Jersey. A federal judge ultimately ruled her appointment was unlawful.

But Habba has been one of the president’s most vocal defenders on conservative outlets. According to the New York Post, citing sources within the administration, Habba is an early frontrunner to replace Leavitt.

Kelly already works at the White House as the principal deputy press secretary, working under Leavitt. She was previously a spokesperson for Trump’s 2024 presidential campaign, and before that she served as national press secretary for the Republican National Committee.

As the wife of Stephen Miller, a top White House aide and immigration policy architect, Katie Miller has a front row seat to the administration’s movements. And as an influential conservative podcast host, Katie has spent a lot of time interviewing cabinet officials and rightwing media figures.

Before launching her podcast, Katie was a communications director for the so-called “department of government efficiency” (Doge). She was vice-president Mike Pence’s press secretary from 2019 to 2021.

Budowich is a former White House deputy chief of staff, who worked alongside Miller and Dan Scavino. He left the White House last year to join the private sector.

Alongside Leavitt, Budowich was one of the defendants in the case brought by the Associated Press after the outlet was banned from the press rotation for refusing to refer to the Gulf of Mexico as the “Gulf of America”.

articles.title: Sudan army says RSF advance on key town bordering Ethiopia
articles.excerpt: Sudan’s Rapid Support Forces and allies of the paramilitary group have advanced into a strategically important town on the Sudanese border with Ethiopia, military and government sources told Al Jazeer...
articles.body_text:
Sudan’s Rapid Support Forces and allies of the paramilitary group have advanced into a strategically important town on the Sudanese border with Ethiopia, military and government sources told Al Jazeera.

They said the RSF and the Sudan People’s Liberation Movement – North (SPLM-N) entered Kurmuk in Blue Nile State on Thursday, as the army began to withdraw.

An RSF statement said an RSF-led coalition had inflicted heavy losses on army troops in Kurmuk, forced them to withdraw and seized weapons and ammunition.

Hours later, the local administration in Kurmuk said the town had come under intensive attacks over the last three days, involving drones and artillery shelling, which it said originated from “the regional neighbourhood”.

The local administration said the Sudanese army continued to confront the attacks “with steadfastness and bravery” in defence of the town, its residents and public institutions.

The town is on an important cross-border route linking Ethiopia with Blue Nile and the wider Nile Valley.

“The RSF advanced into the town with the army withdrawing and repositioning outside,” Al Jazeera’s Almigdad Alruhaid reported from the Sudanese capital Khartoum, citing military and government sources.

The RSF seized the town in March, but the Sudanese army recaptured it last month.

Sudan has been engulfed in its latest conflict since April 2023, when fighting started between the Sudanese army and the RSF over plans to integrate the paramilitary force into the regular military.

The war has killed tens of thousands of people and displaced or forced nearly 15 million to flee their homes, according to UN figures, local authorities and academic estimates.

Elsewhere in Sudan, the army says it repelled an RSF attack on a major town in North Kordofan.

According to military sources who spoke to Al Jazeera, the paramilitary group assaulted the town of Jabra al-Sheikh using heavy artillery and drones. RSF fighters were captured and dozens were killed in the fight, the sources added.

An army statement said the RSF attack involved more than 250 combat vehicles.

Jabra al-Sheikh is a key transport hub in the region and control of the town could allow the RSF to put pressure on el-Obeid – the capital of North Kordofan – and Omdurman near Khartoum.

The latest attacks come the day after the RSF launched far-reaching coordinated drone strikes targeting five army-controlled cities hundreds of kilometres apart.

Wednesday’s attacks killed two people in el-Obeid and paralysed the city’s market, said the rights group Emergency Lawyers that documents atrocities by both sides.

Across Sudan, aid workers estimate that more than 200,000 people have been killed in what the UN calls a “war of atrocities”. The conflict has also caused the world’s largest hunger and displacement crises.

articles.title: Surrogate gives birth in Texas to baby with heart defect after parents requested abortion
articles.excerpt: Fox News correspondent Madeleine Rivera reports on a legal battle involving surrogate mother McKenna West, who traveled to Texas to give birth after refusing the intended parents' request to abort the...
articles.body_text:
Fox News correspondent Madeleine Rivera reports on a legal battle involving surrogate mother McKenna West, who traveled to Texas to give birth after refusing the intended parents' request to abort the baby over a congenital heart condition diagnosis.

A surrogate mother gave birth to a baby against its biological parents' wishes after fleeing to Texas with help from state Attorney General Ken Paxton.

Surrogate mother McKenna West fled to Texas after her baby was diagnosed with hypoplastic left heart syndrome around the time West was 20 weeks pregnant. The diagnosis allegedly prompted the baby's birth parents to ask West to have an abortion, Paxton's office wrote in a Tuesday news release.

After West went on the run to Texas, Paxton intervened, formally notifying UT Southwestern Medical Center and Children’s Medical Center of Dallas of their legal obligations to provide the baby with "medically necessary, life-saving care upon birth," his office wrote.

DEM GOV MAURA HEALEY SIGNS SWEEPING MASSACHUSETTS BILL ALLOWING ABORTIONS UP TO BIRTH

July 29, 2015: Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton speaks during a hearing in Austin, Texas. ( )

"The court has made the right decision in immediately acting to protect baby Gabriel’s life and ensure he receives the care he deserves," Paxton said in the statement. "My office utilized every tool at our disposal to protect life, and we will not back down in continuing to support baby Gabriel’s well-being. Every child in our state deserves to be cared for and protected, and that’s exactly what I’ll fight for."

"While the surrogate mother of baby Gabriel has traveled to Texas for protection and care for Gabriel, the intended parents have refused to agree that they will consent to the life-saving surgery for Gabriel after he is born. Attorney General Paxton has now secured a legal victory that will ensure baby Gabriel’s life is protected and that care is provided," his office's statement also read.

West's baby, named Gabriel, was born on Wednesday, according to Fox News' Kerri Urbahn. Gabriel was brought to a Neonatal Intensive Care Unit where doctors could soon perform lifesaving surgery.

SUPREME COURT UNANIMOUSLY SLAPS DOWN BLUE STATE TARGETING PRO-LIFE GROUP

Surrogate mother McKenna West, who fled to Texas after her baby's birth parents allegedly asked her to abort the child (Live Action)

The hospital where the surgery would likely be performed has a 100% success rate on the procedure, Urbahn reported.

"Baby Gabriel deserves a chance at life, and I will not allow anyone to unlawfully deny him medically necessary care," Paxton said. "My office will use every tool available to protect innocent lives and ensure that every child receives the care required under Texas law."

Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton arrives for the State of the Union address during a Joint Session of Congress at the U.S. Capitol on February 24, 2026, in Washington, DC. (Anna Moneymaker/Getty Images)

Fox News Digital contacted Paxton's office, UT Southwestern Medical Center and Children’s Medical Center of Dallas for additional comment.

articles.title: Socialist insurgency heads to Trump’s backyard, targets pro-Israel Democrat
articles.excerpt: Florida congressional candidate Oliver Larkin faces intense questioning from Sean Hannity over his radical tax policies. During the fiery exchange, the DSA-backed candidate advocates for a return to m...
articles.body_text:
Florida congressional candidate Oliver Larkin faces intense questioning from Sean Hannity over his radical tax policies. During the fiery exchange, the DSA-backed candidate advocates for a return to mid-20th century marginal tax rates and claims that billionaires should be taxed out of existence. Hannity pushes back, defending American innovators and challenging the socialist platform.

The high-stakes battle for the ideological future of the Democratic Party moves to Florida next week, before heading to New England early next month, as the 2026 primary season wraps up.

After impactful left-wing victories this month by Michigan's Abdul El-Sayed and Minnesota Lt. Gov. Peggy Flanagan in crucial Democratic Senate primaries, and a searing setback for the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA), with the downing of DSA member Francesca Hong in Wisconsin's Democratic gubernatorial primary, the next faceoff in the party's civil war comes Tuesday in Florida.

That's where DSA endorsed Oliver Larkin is challenging more moderate Democratic Rep. Jared Moskowitz in a key congressional swing district that's among roughly two dozen House seats that will determine if Republicans hold onto their razor-thin majority in the midterm elections.

DEMOCRATIC GROUP LAUNCHES $15 MILLION WAR ON DEMOCRATIC SOCIALISTS: 'MORTAL DANGER'

Oliver Larkin, a DSA-backed Democratic candidate for Congress in Florida’s 25th district, speaks during a town hall, on May 4, 2026 in Coral Springs, Florida. (Joe Raedle/Getty Images)

Two weeks later, the party's divisions return to a statewide stage, as longtime progressive leader Sen. Ed Markey of Massachusetts is facing a serious primary challenge from more moderate Democratic Rep. Seth Moulton.

A left-versus-center battle is brewing a week later in neighboring New Hampshire, in the party's Senate primary for a crucial battleground seat Democrats must hold in the midterm elections in order to win back the chamber's majority from the GOP.

Progressives scored their biggest victory to date a week ago, when El-Sayed narrowly edged moderate Rep. Haley Stevens to capture the party's Senate nomination in the Great Lakes battleground, in the race to succeed retiring Democratic Sen. Gary Peters.

DEMOCRATIC GROUP LAUNCHES $15 MILLION WAR ON DEMOCRATIC SOCIALISTS: 'MORTAL DANGER'

Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed speaks to supporters at an election-night rally at the Majestic Theatre in Detroit, Mich., on Aug. 4, 2026. His race against U.S. Rep. Haley Stevens in the state Democratic primary ended too close to call. (Getty Images)

On Tuesday, Flanagan downed moderate Democratic Rep. Angie Craig by roughly 20 points, to grab the party's nomination in blue-leaning but competitive Minnesota, in the race to succeed another retiring Democrat, Sen. Tina Smith.

Both El-Sayed and Flanagan were backed by top far-left leaders, including progressive champion Sen. Bernie Sanders of Vermont.

But in Wisconsin's Democratic gubernatorial showdown, Hong was upset by a razor-thin margin by Milwaukee County Executive David Crowley, who was backed by retiring Democratic Gov. Tony Evers.

Evers and Crowley, pointing to Hong's past controversial comments on defunding the police and criticizing Thanksgiving, argued that a Hong primary victory would have boosted GOP nominee Rep. Tom Tiffany's chances of flipping the Wisconsin governor's mansion.

With the primary calendar winding down, here's a closer look at the final nomination faceoffs that are dividing Democrats and giving Republicans plenty of ammunition to use in the midterms.

The 33-year-old Larkin, a veteran of Sanders' 2016 Democratic presidential campaign, is also the only DSA-endorsed House candidate running in a crucial congressional swing district.

Larkin says he supports abolishing the U.S. Senate, arguing in a Fox News interview that it's an "undemocratic institution."

He agreed with socialist New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani that Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu should have been arrested during his recent trip to the U.S., and refers to Israel's ruling coalition as a "religious supremacist regime."

Moskowitz is a strong and vocal supporter of Israel, who has advocated for robust U.S. military and security assistance.

DEMOCRACY ’26: STAY UP TO DATE WITH THE FOX NEWS ELECTION HUB

Rep. Jared Moskowitz, a Democrat from Florida, faces a primary challenge from the far-left as he runs for re-election in 2026. (Al Drago/Bloomberg via Getty Images)

The two-term federal lawmaker and former state representative and Florida FEMA director is running for re-election in the state's newly redrawn 25th Congressional District, a Broward County-anchored seat in the southeastern corner of the red-leaning state

Moskowitz, who enjoys establishment backing from the Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee, is also supported by AIPAC, a major-Israel aligned political group. Larkin enjoys plenty of support from top far-left leaders, including controversial political streamer Hasan Piker. Moskowitz is the polling and fundraising lead over Larkin heading into the primary.

Markey is backed by a slew of progressive politicians and groups, including Sanders and Sen. Elizabeth Warren of Massachusetts, as well as fellow Bay Stater Rep. Ayanna Pressley, a member of the far-left Squad.

Sen. Ed Markey of Massachusetts is backed by progressive champions Sens. Bernie Sanders and Elizabeth Warren as he faces a Democratic primary challenge from Rep. Seth Moulton. (Jemal Countess/Getty Images for MoveOn Civic Action)

Moulton is supported by a smaller group of more moderate Democratic lawmakers and groups.

While the primary is partially viewed as a progressive versus moderate showdown, the Democratic Party's generational showdown is very much at play in this contest.

The 80-year-old Markey has served in Congress for half a century, first in the House and since 2013 in the Senate. The 47-year-old Moulton has repeatedly emphasized it's time for a new generation of leaders.

Democratic Rep. Seth Moulton of Massachusetts is primary challenging Sen. Ed Markey in the 2026 election cycle. (Samuel Corum/Getty Images)

The push by Democrats for generational change was fueled two years ago by then-81-year-old President Joe Biden's exit from the presidential race amid questions over his physical and mental stamina following a disastrous debate performance against President Donald Trump.

A similar generational fight is being waged in the Democratic primary in Massachusetts' 8th Congressional District. That's where 71-year-old Rep. Stephen Lynch, who has served in the House for a quarter-century, is being primary challenged by 39-year-old Patrick Roath.

The action moves north a week later to neighboring New Hampshire, where longtime Democratic Sen. Jeanne Shaheen, the first woman in the nation's history elected governor and to the Senate, is retiring.

Four-term Rep. Chris Pappas is the front-runner for the Democratic nomination, and enjoys plenty of establishment backing, including from Shaheen and the Granite State's other Democrat in the chamber, Sen. Maggie Hassan.

Democratic Senate candidate in New Hampshire Rep. Chris Pappas is interviewed by Fox News Digital, on July 4, 2025, in Portsmouth, N.H. (Paul Steinhauser - Fox News)

Pappas is the clear polling and fundraising leader in a race that also includes medical scientist Karishma Manzur, who is backed by a handful of progressive groups.

A backer of Israel, Pappas has been blasted over the support he's receiving from AIPAC by Manzur, who argues Israeli has committed "genocide" against Palestinians in its war with Hamas in Gaza.

Fox News' Matthew Donnell contributed to this report.

Paul Steinhauser covers the national campaign trail from coast to coast for Fox News

articles.title: Luxury $9 million yacht caught on camera sinking off coast, days after delivery to owner
articles.excerpt:
The Angiola II sank off the island of Porto Cervo, Sardinia, after an engine fire. (Credit: Jam Press)

A super-luxury $9.1 million yacht sank into the waters of the Mediterranean Sea on Tuesday, just...
articles.body_text:
The Angiola II sank off the island of Porto Cervo, Sardinia, after an engine fire. (Credit: Jam Press)

A super-luxury $9.1 million yacht sank into the waters of the Mediterranean Sea on Tuesday, just days after it had been delivered to its new owner.

The Angiola II was off the coast of Porto Cervo on the popular Italian island of Sardinia with 14 guests on board, when it experienced engine failure that sparked a fire, the New York Post reported.

DRUNK REPEAT OFFENDER CALLED A 'TICKING TIME-BOMB' BEFORE 80-MPH BOATING COLLISION KILLED WOMAN: PROSECUTORS

The Angiola II, a $9.1 million luxury yacht, sank Tuesday in the Mediterranean Sea just days after it had been delivered to its new owner. (Jam Press)

The blaze damaged seals on the vessel, which began to take on water, causing it to tip onto its side. The guests managed to escape to safety and were rescued by nearby vessels, The Telegraph reported.

Video footage taken at the scene shows the boat on its side.

COAST GUARD OPENS FIRE ON BOAT SMUGGLING 25 CHINESE NATIONALS NEAR FLORIDA AFTER IT REFUSED TO STOP

A $9.1 million superyacht sinks in waters off Porto Cervo, Sardinia, just four days after being delivered to its Italian owner. The Angiola II, a nearly 30-meter vessel, lost buoyancy following an engine failure that caused a fire in the seals, allowing water to enter the hull. (Jam Press)

The unidentified owner — an Italian businessman — was the last one off the ship, the newspaper reported.

The yacht reportedly sank at a depth of around 23 feet between an island called L’Isola dei Cappuccini and Capo Ferro, on Sardinia’s exclusive Costa Smeralda, or Emerald Coast, the news report states.

The boat will be kept under surveillance until a recovery company recovers it from the sea floor.

The superyacht sank in the Mediterranean Sea off Porto Cervo, Sardinia. Fourteen people were on board; 12 were rescued by a nearby vessel, while the owner and a friend remained on the yacht until a patrol boat transported them to Poltu Quatu. No injuries were reported. (Jam Press)

The yacht can reportedly accommodate 10 guests and is fitted with five cabins and five crew members.

It has four engines and can reach speeds of 28 knots.

Louis Casiano is a reporter for Fox News Digital. Story tips can be sent to louis.casiano@fox.com.

articles.title: Baseball fans fume at MLB's 'Field of Dreams' game decision, reporter Tricia Whitaker has a boat day & LLWS!
articles.excerpt:
Three fans ran onto the field at Yankee Stadium on Wednesday and were promptly wrestled to the ground in a chaotic scene. (This video contains AI-assisted content)

'Nightcaps' is a daily column that ...
articles.body_text:
Three fans ran onto the field at Yankee Stadium on Wednesday and were promptly wrestled to the ground in a chaotic scene. (This video contains AI-assisted content)

'Nightcaps' is a daily column that catches you up on the biggest sports, news and culture stories you may have missed while pretending to do work at your desk. It runs Monday–Friday on OutKick.com.

Over the hump and safely into a big Thursday filled with actual NFL football (kind of) and an MLB Field of Dreams game only the 1%ers can watch.

What a blessing. What a day! Are things starting to ramp up, or what? And who knows! Maybe by the end of this class, the WNBA will have figured out what a woman is.

HOME RUN DERBY RATINGS CRASH ON NETFLIX, SETS 20-PLUS-YEAR LOW AS QUESTIONS SURFACE ABOUT PROGRAM QUALITY

I wouldn't hold your breath, but there's always a chance.

Welcome to a Thursday Nightcaps — the one where Pat Sajak, of all people, points out the lunacy in tonight's annual Field of Dreams game.

Players from the Chicago White Sox and New York Yankees walk through the corn rows before a game at Field of Dreams in Dyersville, Iowa, on Aug. 12, 2021. (Getty Images)

Pat Sajak! We usually only check in with Maggie Sajak in this class. I believe Pat's a first-timer. Welcome aboard!

What else? I've got a couple wild moments yesterday in the world of little league baseball, Apple TV's Tricia Whitaker enjoyed a Canadian cottage getaway and Lordy, did you guys have some steak takes on the heels of yesterday's class.

Take out a second mortgage, grab you a Netflix subscription and settle in for a Thursday 'Cap!

I think Major League Baseball does a lot of things right. Frankly, they're probably the best sport when it comes to doing things that make sense.

Look at the mess that is the WNBA right now and compare it to MLB. It's laughable.

The pitch clock was brilliant. I've come around on the ghost runner. ABS has very clearly worked. The Home Run Derby and the All-Star game are the two best exhibition events in sports (not a high bar, to be fair).

The Field of Dreams game has been a home run since its debut way back in 2021. It's perfect. Everything about it is perfect.

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

This year — tonight — is the first year it won't be on Fox. Instead, it was scooped up by Netflix during last year's TV negotiations.

Yes, that means if you really want to watch some Phillies-Twins action tonight from Iowa, you're gonna have to pay up.

Does it seem a bit ironic that MLB’s Field of Dreams game — which harkens back to a simpler, more bucolic time — is being streamed on Netflix?

You know what, Pat Sajak? You are 1000% right. What a rip-off! More importantly, what a vocabulary on 79-year-old Pat Sajak! Bucolic? I'm not sure I've ever seen that word in my life. Does Pat still have the fastball, or what?

Bucolic, by the way, is an adjective that means relating to the pleasant, peaceful aspects of the countryside, country life, or shepherds, according to the stupid AI bot that runs Google now.

Pat wasn't alone in his bewilderment, by the way:

I could go on and on. Nobody is happy. Is anyone ever happy?

For those still on the fence, a Netflix subscription costs $8.99 a month (with ads). If you really hate ads, you have to pony up a whopping $20 a month. And if you really hate ads AND regular 1080p HD, you have to pay $27 for the 4K version.

Thank God I'm a T-Mobile customer. Free MLB TV and Netflix included! What a deal.

(Not a promotion, but I wouldn't mind if it was.)

Aaron Judge #99 of the New York Yankees hits a three-run home run in the third inning during a game against the Chicago White Sox at the MLB Field at Field of Dreams on Thursday, Aug. 12, 2021, in Dyersville, Iowa. (MLB Photos via Getty Images)

OK, let's keep this class moving ... from the big diamond to the little diamond! What a night we had in the Little League World Series regionals last night.

The coach who gave a sermon on the mound (come on, that's a good one!) is taking a little heat today because folks say he should've been out there giving a scouting report instead. Boots on the ground say the next three batters reached safely, and Arizona went on to lose.

Not great! For what it's worth, my little league coach used to tell me, "Zach, if you strike out, there are a billion people in China who will wake up tomorrow and won't care."

Decent advise for a 12-year-old, I reckon. But we also never got anywhere close to Williamsport, so perhaps we could've used some more motivation.

Garrett Gallegos #19 of the Mountain Region from Las Vegas, Nevada reacts before the sixth inning against the Asia-Pacific Region team from Taoyuan City, Chinese Taipei during the 2025 Little League World Series Championship at Howard J. Lamade Stadium on Aug. 24, 2025, in South Williamsport, Pa. (Getty Images)

As for the coach who got tossed ... that's nothing. I grew up with a coach who used to get thrown out every week for arguing anything and everything under the sun. During one All-Star game in particular, he snuck back into the complex Bobby Valentine style and hung out behind the outfield fence.

That's called commitment. Loved Coach Tony.

OK, let's rapid-fire this Thursday class into a big Thursday night of preseason football. First up? Yesterday, I gave you my Mount Rushmore of Steaks to celebrate National Filet Mignon Day.

Anything that moos is my favorite meat. I grew up a meat and potatoes kid. Still am 7 decades later. Ribeyes and Kansas City strips are my favorites. My smoker will be fired up this weekend.

Thanks, Larry! Bring a couple over to the Field of Dreams game!

Ribeye on the bone — the bone must be there with no questions asked – it’s not the same eating a boneless ribeye.

Porterhouse — which you cannot go wrong, and it is of course two steaks in one on a big bone — so technically, number 2 and 3 would equal a porterhouse.

Thanks, Tom! Agree wholeheartedly on the bone-in Ribeye. Huge difference.

Agree with your steak rankings. Up until end of last year I never even considered ordering anything but a ribeye, but I’ve been on a filet tear so far this year. For me it’s more about portion control than anything else. I can’t be knocking down 14+ oz ribeyes all the time anymore.

It's football season, Ryan. Portion control, shmortion control! Let's get the ribeyes back in the rotation and worry about the waistline in January.

OK, that's it for today. Good work, everyone. Six NFL preseason games tonight and the Field of Dreams game for those who have a rich uncle who recently kicked the bucket.

Here's Apple TV's MLB girl, Tricia Whitaker, to get everyone ready.

Best little league memories? Email me at Zach.Dean@OutKick.com.

articles.title: Hasan Piker event cancellation sparks intervention from top House progressive
articles.excerpt:
Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed complained about cancel culture when pressed on his association with far-left streamer Hasan Piker, after denouncing the streamer's 9/11 remarks.

A top House ...
articles.body_text:
Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed complained about cancel culture when pressed on his association with far-left streamer Hasan Piker, after denouncing the streamer's 9/11 remarks.

A top House Democrat is speaking out against a university's decision to cancel an appearance by controversial far-left activist Hasan Piker on its campus.

Rep. Pramila Jayapal, D-Wash., the former Congressional Progressive Caucus chair, publicly called on students at the University of Washington to "work with the university to ensure" that Piker was able to speak.

Jayapal also said in a statement posted to X on Thursday that she was personally working with the university on the issue.

DEMOCRATIC INFIGHTING GROWS AS CONGRESSWOMAN EXPOSES ‘DISRESPECTFUL’ WELCOME OF SOCIALISTS INTO ‘BIG TENT’

Rep. Pramila Jayapal is speaking out against the University of Washington's decision to cancel Hasan Piker's speaking engagement. (Noushad Variyattiyakkal/SOPA Images/LightRocket via Getty Images; Anna Moneymaker/Getty Images)

"As a Member of the Judiciary Committee, I have been absolutely clear that free speech is a constitutional right that we must all stand up and protect. I have been communicating my concerns about the cancellation of the Hasan Piker event directly to the University, and they have informed me that they are doing an internal review to ensure this never happens again," Jayapal wrote.

Piker posted on X earlier this week that the event was canceled due to his criticism of Israel.

"i wish the dems were smarter & didn’t let the [right-wing] groups be the only people who speak out against this clear violation of [the First Amendment] but unfortunately my position as a prominent critic of israel stops them from using this moment to show gop as arch cancel culture warriors," Piker wrote.

The University of Washington faced bipartisan criticism for canceling Piker's appearance. (Karen Ducey/Getty Images)

The University of Washington said in a statement that Piker's event was canceled because it "was determined that the process for organizing this event did not meet the necessary level of rigor for University-hosted events."

The decision also prompted backlash from the right.

"Let the radical Mao loving communist Hasan Piker speak, so long as he can resist the urge to call for the death of his political opponents. Universities do this to TPUSA often and blame some admin error etc.," Turning Point USA's Andrew Kolvet posted on X. "It’s wrong. Let him speak. Let conservatives speak. Peacefully."

Piker, a streamer, has long made headlines for controversial and far-left statements.

In 2019, he said "America deserved 9/11" over its foreign policy decisions, though he later walked it back on "The Young Turks," stating, "Every part of what I advocate for is against violence" and insisting his statement was misconstrued.

HASAN PIKER'S DEFENSE OF HAMAS HAVING 'RIGHT TO RESIST MILITARILY' DRAWS CONDEMNATION FROM HUMAN RIGHTS GROUPS

Piker said at a Yale University event in April 2026 that "the fall of the USSR was one of the greatest catastrophes of the 20th century."

Abdul El-Sayed, a progressive candidate who won the Democratic primary for U.S. Senate in Michigan, talks poolside with streamer Hasan Piker at a party for content creators supporting his campaign on Aug. 3, 2026, in Detroit. (Julia Demaree Nikhinson/AP Photo)

He also drew backlash from the Anti-Defamation League for calling terror group Hamas a "lesser evil" compared to Israel.

The far-left activist and his past statements have been back in the national conversation in recent weeks as he campaigns with socialist-aligned candidates across the country. That includes Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed and failed Wisconsin gubernatorial candidate Francesca Hong.

Fox News Digital reached out to Piker for comment on Jayapal's and Kolvet's defense of his speaking engagement.

Elizabeth Elkind is a politics reporter for Fox News Digital leading coverage of the House of Representatives. Previous digital bylines seen at Daily Mail and CBS News.

Follow on Twitter at @liz_elkind and send tips to elizabeth.elkind@fox.com

articles.title: Chicago Bears say 'sole focus' is building new stadium in Indiana and reveal how that will affect their name
articles.excerpt:
Indiana Gov. Mike Braun details the Chicago Bears’ likely move to Indiana, touts public safety in his state and more on ‘Fox & Friends Weekend.’

The Chicago Bears on Thursday announced that their new...
articles.body_text:
Indiana Gov. Mike Braun details the Chicago Bears’ likely move to Indiana, touts public safety in his state and more on ‘Fox & Friends Weekend.’

The Chicago Bears on Thursday announced that their new stadium planning and expectations, which the team had been balancing between options in Arlington Heights, Illinois and Hammond Indiana, will now have a "sole focus" on the site in the state next door.

The club is definitely leaving Chicago, which it has called home since 1921.

And it is almost definitely leaving Illinois, too.

CHICAGO BEARS TAKE MAJOR STEP TOWARD LEAVING CITY AFTER MORE THAN A CENTURY AS FRANCHISE MAKES INDIANA PLANS

"...Even though we've had occasional meetings with the state of Illinois, our sole focus at this point in time is working on a world-class stadium and mixed use development in Hammond, Indiana," Bears CEO Kevin Warren told reporters on Thursday.

Jan 17, 2023; Chicago, Illinois, US; Chicago Bears chairman George H. McCaskey speaks as he introduces new Chicago Bears president and CEO Kevin Warren during the press conference at Halas Hall. (Kamil Krzaczynski-USA TODAY Sports)

"We will be the Chicago Bears, whether we're in Arlington or whether we're in Hammond," Bears Chairman George McCaskey said. "And as Kevin said, our focus on Hammond, that's where we're advancing our efforts, and that's where the bulk of our time, attention, and resources are being devoted."

McCaskey said he understands there is anxiety from Bears fans that the club is likely leaving the state.

Fans cheer before the game between the Chicago Bears and the Los Angeles Rams in the NFC Divisional Playoffs at Soldier Field on Jan. 18, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Michael Reaves/Getty Images)

"We understand that that's out there," he said. "And it needs to be dealt with. We are doing surveying, research, data collection, to address those issues. And as I said months ago, this is going to require an adjustment.

"But it required an adjustment when we went from Wrigley [Field] to Soldier [Field]. It required an adjustment when we went from, Soldier to Champaign temporarily. And it required an adjustment when we came back to the quote unquote new Soldier Field.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

"That's how it works over the course of 100-years-plus of franchise stewardship."

For months there has been hope among some fans and others in Illinois that some sort of Hail Mary proposal or scheme could somehow keep the Bears from bolting. That would require work with the mostly Democrat politicians in Illinois from Gov. J.B. Pritzker to legislators and McCaskey made it clear those discussions with Illinois politicians haven't been fruitful.

Illinois Gov. JB Pritzker holds a news conference with other Illinois politicians and community leaders to address President Donald Trump's plan to send National Guard troops into Chicago on Aug. 25, 2025 in Chicago, Ill. (Scott Olson/Getty Images)

"Minimal," McCaskey said describing the communication. "We were waiting to see whether there would be some substantive action taken. We thought we had presented a pretty compelling case that a stadium in Arlington would be beneficial not only for the village of Arlington Heights, but for the community, and for the entire state.

"Really a tremendous driver of economic activity, job creation, tax revenue, sales revenue, and ultimately that argument was unsuccessful."

CHICAGO POLITICIANS ARE DOING WINDY CITY POLITICIAN THINGS TO TRY TO KEEP THE BEARS IN TOWN

The mostly Republican politicians in Indiana, meanwhile, have offered a stark contrast.

"The representatives from the state of Indiana, all the way from the governor's office to representatives in Northwest Indiana, have been phenomenal partners," Warren said. "They've been stellar to work with, very professional, diligent, with a can-do attitude."

FOLLOW ARMANDO SALGUERO ON X: @ARMANDOSALGUERO

Armando Salguero is OutKick's Senior NFL Writer.

articles.title: Prichard Colon, boxer left in vegetative state after illegal punches in 2015 bout, dead at 33
articles.excerpt:
Rising boxing star Conor Benn talks to Fox News Digital about his deal with Zuffa Boxing.

Prichard Colon, the former boxer who fell into a coma in 2015 following a controversial match, has died. He w...
articles.body_text:
Rising boxing star Conor Benn talks to Fox News Digital about his deal with Zuffa Boxing.

Prichard Colon, the former boxer who fell into a coma in 2015 following a controversial match, has died. He was 33.

The news was shared by Colon’s father, Richard, on Thursday, announcing the heartbreaking news about his son.

"Good morning, my people. I regret to inform you of the passing of my son Prichard from this earthly world," he wrote on Facebook, translated from Spanish. "Now he is in a better world.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

Prichard Colon looks on against Terrel Williams in their super welterweight bout at EagleBank Arena on the campus of George Mason University in Fairfax, Va., on Oct. 17, 2015. (Getty Images)

"I did everything possible to fulfill his wish, his dream of bringing him on vacation on Puerto Rico as much as he desired, but couldn’t. Thank you for so many years of love and prayers. As much as you can, please keep us in your prayers."

Colon was one of boxing’s rising stars in 2015, owning a 16-0 record with 13 knockouts to his name ahead of his fight to Terrel Williams.

BOXER PRICHARD COLÓN TAKEN OFF SEDATIVES, FAMILY PRAYS HE WAKES FROM COMA

But during that bout, Colon was repeatedly hit in the back of the head by illegal punches. He tried telling the referee about it, but the fight continued on.

While Williams wasn’t docked for the illegal hits, Colon was hit with a two-point penalty for a low blow on his opponent.

In the end, Colon hit the canvas in the ninth round, and his team removed his gloves while he was down thinking the fight was over. It, in fact, wasn’t and Colon was disqualified.

Prichard Colon weighs in on July 31, 2015, at Barclays Center in Brooklyn, N.Y. (Getty Images)

However, a more serious situation occurred when he needed help getting to the locker room. He vomited and collapsed, immediately leading to his team getting him to the hospital.

Colon was diagnosed with a subdural hematoma, and he underwent an emergency procedure to reduce brain swelling.

As a result, Colon fell into a coma that lasted 221 days. Upon waking up, he was in a vegetative state, unable to speak without using a computer.

STAY "FEARLESS" ON THE GO! TAKE TOMI LAHREN WITH YOU. DOWNLOAD THE TLIF PODCAST NOW!

Colon needed to be cared for by his family up until his death.

Prichard Colon celebrates his win over Daniel Calzada during a Premier Boxing Champions junior middleweight bout at Barclays Center in Brooklyn, N.Y., on April 11, 2015. (Getty Images)

Colon finished his boxing career as an honorary WBC World Champion and a gold medal winner at the 2010 Pan American Youth Championship in the 64 kilogram weight class.

Follow Fox News Digital’s sports coverage on X and subscribe to the Fox News Sports Huddle newsletter.

Scott Thompson is a sports writer for Fox News Digital.

The death of Rob Delaney's son, Henry, fundamentally changed the way he approaches Hollywood, prompting the "Deadpool" star to limit...
articles.body_text:
Fox News Flash top entertainment and celebrity headlines are here.

The death of Rob Delaney's son, Henry, fundamentally changed the way he approaches Hollywood, prompting the "Deadpool" star to limit his workload and spend as much time as possible at home with his children.

Delaney lost his two-and-a-half-year-old son in 2018 after battling a brain tumor. Henry had been diagnosed with cancer shortly after his 1st birthday.

"I had a son, his name was Henry, and he died, and he's dead," he said during an appearance on Ted Danson's podcast, "Where Everybody Knows Your Name." "You know, does he live on inside of me and in the smile of my wife and in the gaze of my other boys who are alive and vibrant? Yes, he does. But he died, and I don't like to sugarcoat that, you know. And that affected how I work now."

RYAN GOSLING'S FAMILY-FIRST PHILOSOPHY RESHAPED HIS HOLLYWOOD CAREER: EXPERTS

Rob Delaney said the death of his son Henry in 2018 reshaped the way he approaches his Hollywood career. (Imeh Akpanudosen/Getty Images)

Rather than building a production empire or juggling numerous projects like some peers, he chose to prioritize being physically present with his family.

"...they've got their fingers in other pies," he said. "I don't do that. I just do one, maybe two things at a time to the best of my abilities, and then I just spend the rest of the time at home, you know, smelling my kids and having as many of them sit on me at one time as possible, you know."

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER

The "Deadpool" star said he limits himself to one or two projects at a time to prioritize time with his family. (Frazer Harrison/Getty Images)

For Delaney, that shift in priorities is inseparable from the grief he continues to carry.

"That's a big part of me is metabolizing that the pain of the loss of Henry and then trying to be smart enough to let that inform how I do my career, because I think it would be a real shame if that happened and I didn't change how I work, you know," he explained. "That would be folly."

Delaney spent years working in stand-up before gaining a major following on Twitter, where his offbeat comedy helped turn him into one of the platform’s earliest breakout comedians. In 2012, he was named "Funniest Person on Twitter" at Comedy Central’s Comedy Awards.

Rob Delaney said the grief of losing Henry continues to inform how he balances work and fatherhood. (Bryan Bedder/Getty Images)

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

Rob Delaney found a major following through stand-up, Twitter and his acclaimed series "Catastrophe." (Allen J. Schaben/Los Angeles Times via Getty Images)

His biggest career breakthrough came with "Catastrophe," the acclaimed comedy series he co-created, co-wrote and starred in alongside Sharon Horgan from 2015 to 2019.

Some of Delaney's biggest roles include "Deadpool 2", "Mission: Impossible – Dead Reckoning Part One," "Deadpool & Wolverine" and "Dying for Sex."

articles.title: Colombia earthquake: Hospitals adapt to save lives amid widespread damage
articles.excerpt: Cali, Colombia – At the University Hospital of the Valle Evaristo Garcia, health workers in blue scrubs moved briskly through the courtyard on Wednesday, beneath a white facade split by deep fissures....
articles.body_text:
Cali, Colombia – At the University Hospital of the Valle Evaristo Garcia, health workers in blue scrubs moved briskly through the courtyard on Wednesday, beneath a white facade split by deep fissures.

The rear of the hospital – a major public medical centre in Colombia’s Cali – had partially collapsed on Monday, after a magnitude 7.4 earthquake struck the west of the country, killing at least 273 people and injuring at least 3,800 others. The National Unit for Disaster Risk Management said 377 people are still missing as the crucial three-day rescue window passes.

Carlos Naranjo, a general practitioner at the hospital, said some 50 percent of the facility was damaged. “There is extensive structural damage; some walls are no longer stable, some ceilings have collapsed, and it is still dangerous to walk through,” he told Al Jazeera.

With most of the hospital off-limits, medical staff now have to turn away the vast majority of patients. They are able to treat only those who require immediate resuscitation.

The facility is one of four major hospitals that were damaged and forced out of operation on Monday. Six clinics were also damaged. Amid an influx of injured people, city authorities on Monday warned that public hospitals in Cali, home to two million people, were at 100 percent capacity and declared a “red alert for hospitals” there.

Cali, Colombia’s third-largest city and the capital of the Valle del Cauca province in the Pacific region, is one of the worst-affected areas.

At least 96 died here, while 1,224 others were injured and 111 are officially missing. Authorities say some 45 buildings collapsed, while 832 suffered damage.

But on Wednesday – less than 72 hours into the crisis – a combination of effective organisation, plentiful volunteers, and support from the national government has led local health officials to describe the situation as stable.

The United Nations’ Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) said on Wednesday that the “hospital system has stabilised as patients have been discharged and the number of new admissions has decreased”.

But “a red alert remains declared for hospitals in the city”, it said.

The city averted disaster despite the collapse of key health institutions by enacting a strategy to boost the capacity of the institutions less affected by the earthquake, officials said.

German Escobar, Cali’s public health secretary, told Al Jazeera that the city had implemented a plan to create “expansion zones”, largely in and around existing health institutions, to handle the surge in patients.

These include utilising operating rooms that were previously not in use and recovery areas – where patients go after surgery – that were partially or fully closed before the earthquake.

In other hospitals – like the private Clinica Nuestra – the expansion zones come in the form of temporary field clinics.

The hospital was forced to relocate patients after a partial collapse.

Here, an ambulance lies crushed by fallen debris, with a buckled “Emergency Room” sign hanging loosely above it.

“The situation is now stable,” Escobar said.

He noted that while there is still stress on the healthcare system, particularly for patients with chronic illnesses struggling to access medications, the threat of hospitals being overwhelmed and unable to attend to those in need has now been contained.

“Unless another major mass event occurs that overwhelms emergency and inpatient services, the system should be fully stabilised,” he added.

The health secretary credited the recovery of the city’s hospital system to successful coordination between government officials, relief organisations and volunteers.

Relief efforts also depended on vast resources and manpower from civil society organisations.

Enrique Zapata, head of logistics at Cali-based health NGO SARES, stood in front of a crowded medical tent at the foot of the Vanessa apartment – a six-storey building that collapsed on August 10. The medical tent primarily serves volunteers, treating them as they carry out rescue operations.

As rescuers hurried past carrying buckets and shovels, he described the first moments after the earthquake.

“Everyone first checked on their family, and after that, all of us who are first responders, we immediately got in touch with the organisations we belong to,” said the medic.

He explained that emergency responders followed a plan, named the Incident Command System, which guided their immediate response – a system set up in advance to prepare for disasters that coordinates how government agencies and civil society groups can work together in the event of disasters.

“Personally, I think the city was well-prepared,” Zapata told Al Jazeera.

Beyond protocol, rescue workers were spurred to work through the night by a sense of duty.

“Even though your body often tells you, ‘I want to rest’, the adrenaline and the desire to help keep you from doing so,” explained Zapata.

Ricardo Castillo, an army veteran volunteering as a nurse at another collapse site in Cali, described a similar mobilisation.

“The work of the people in charge of all this has been spectacular,” he said.

Behind him, volunteers worked alongside firefighters, police and military personnel among the shattered concrete and metal rebar, removing debris in buckets by passing them hand to hand along chains of rescuers.

“The support is infinite. These people are wonderful,” added Castillo.

The quake’s timing and location – just weeks after magnitude 7.2 and 7.5 earthquakes struck neighbouring Venezuela on June 24 – has prompted comparisons between the two countries’ responses.

The scale of the disaster in Venezuela was far greater than in Colombia, with more than 6,000 killed.

Venezuela’s government has faced sharp criticism over its response, with survivors saying help never arrived in the crucial first hours and days. Civilians led much of the relief effort, especially in the first two days, while delayed orders from senior military commanders and widespread confusion hampered the deployment of troops, according to media reports.

“It is inevitable to compare the responses of both countries,” said Marianella Herrera, Director of the Caracas-based Venezuelan Health Observatory.

“In one country, there is clearly a much more coordinated and coherent response, while in the other – which is, of course, Venezuela – the response is much more fragmented from an institutional standpoint.”

While Herrera noted a great deal of solidarity and support from the Venezuelan population, she blamed inadequate coordination within the country’s health system for the comparatively poor response to the tragedy.

“The lack of organisation and leadership in the Venezuelan healthcare system exacerbates a situation that calls for a well-coordinated and robust healthcare system,” said the health expert.

Venezuelan authorities have rejected criticism of their response as the product of “media laboratories”.

In Cali, rescuers say the crisis is far from over. With dozens still missing in the city and more than 500 officially recorded as missing nationwide, health workers say the emergency is unlikely to ease anytime soon.

Emergency workers are still calling for all the help they can get.

“In these situations, there is no such thing as too much. Every little helps,” said Castillo

articles.title: Donald Trump empowers US private companies to conduct cyber-attacks
articles.excerpt:
President signed memorandum giving private sector a role in fighting ‘transnational criminal organizations’

Donald Trump signed a memo on Wednesday that aims to give private companies the power to ca...
articles.body_text:
President signed memorandum giving private sector a role in fighting ‘transnational criminal organizations’

Donald Trump signed a memo on Wednesday that aims to give private companies the power to carry out offensive cyber-attacks against foreign criminal entities.

The president ⁠signed a ​national security presidential memorandum directing his administration to “leverage the capability and innovation of the private sector to help conduct these ⁠cyber operations under the direction, control and authority of the US government”, the White House said.

The policy shift gives the private sector a role that has traditionally been reserved for government agencies, essentially deputizing companies in the fight against crime online. Trump’s memo does not give private firms unlimited ability to conduct hacking operations, but instead would authorize “limited cyber operations at the direction of the US government”.

International concern over cyber-attacks has grown after the release of increasingly powerful artificial intelligence models, which have shown that they can hack into outdated security systems. In the US, hackers targeted critical infrastructure systems in several states earlier this year, resulting in disruptions at water facilities.

The White House, in a fact sheet about ⁠the memo, cited ransomware attacks, financial frauds and other crimes run by foreign-based criminal organizations, ​referred to in the memo ‌as “transnational criminal organizations” (TCOs).

The Trump administration has previously vowed to give private firms a larger role in cybersecurity operations. A national cybersecurity policy released in March stated that the government would create incentives to “unleash the private sector” against foreign adversaries. These plans have faced questions from legal experts on what sort of risks companies could face as they enmesh themselves in international digital conflicts.

The memo, released on Wednesday, ‌creates a framework that encourages private sector companies to enter into agreements with other ‌private entities, as well as federal, state, local, tribal and territorial agencies, to gather threat information on transnational criminal organizations and propose cyber operations to address those threats, the White House added.

The memo directs the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), through the homeland security taskforce’s national coordination center, to create a program “to conduct specific ‌cyber operations that disrupt foreign TCOs” that will be overseen by the DHS and the Department of Justice.

Under the supervision of the federal government, participating ​companies, once vetted, will conduct “cyber surveillance operations” and “cyber effects operations” against specified targets, according to the memo.

“Cyber effects includes the potential manipulation, disruption, denial, degradation or destruction of information systems, networks, physical or virtual infrastructure controlled by information systems, or information resident thereon,” according to the ⁠memo.

Participating companies will have to maintain a bond or escrow of ​at least $1m, according ​to the memo.

The idea of ​private sector firms participating in cyber operations against criminal and other ​targets is not ‌new but has encountered ​controversy in ​the past over fears of escalation, inadvertent consequences and inter-agency coordination issues.

The DHS and the White House did not immediately respond to requests for additional details about the program.

articles.title: DiJonai Carrington reportedly had fan escorted from his seat over an 'unfounded' accusation

Wednesday night, DiJonai Carringto...
articles.body_text:
Dan Dakich breaks down the hypocrisy surrounding the WNBA and the Indiana Fever as Caitlin Clark and Sophie Cunningham step up to defend head coach Stephanie White.

Wednesday night, DiJonai Carrington slapped two players across the face, received a technical foul, shot 1-for-9 from the field and had an innocent fan removed from the game.

For more details on that final point, the New York Post reports that Carrington complained to officials during the fourth quarter of the Sky-Valkyries game about a fan sitting near the court. The fan was then escorted away from his seat, only to return later after Carrington's complaint was deemed "unfounded."

"The fan was cooperative after a complaint that was unfounded," a Valkyries official told ClutchPoints.

DIJONAI CARRINGTON, WHO DECLARED 'WHITE PRIVILEGE' AFTER EJECTION, PLAYS VS STORM AS WNBA REMAINS SILENT

Chicago Sky's DiJonai Carrington walks off the court after being ejected for a flagrant foul against Indiana Fever's Sophie Cunningham during the first half of a WNBA basketball game in Chicago on Saturday, Aug. 8, 2026. (AP Photo/Paul Beaty)

It's unclear what Carrington accused the fan of saying. The USA Network broadcast captured part of the incident during the game.

"So, there is a stoppage right now as Chicago’s team security has stepped out along with arena security representatives," the broadcast informed viewers.

"Carrington went over to one of the officials, as you see Sarah Williams there, to say something."

Put simply, DiJonai Carrington does not get the benefit of the doubt. She lost that.

She continues to conduct herself like a professional victim. This was the case even before she clotheslined Sophie Cunningham, posted "white privilege" on social media from the locker room and then claimed her accusation of racism wasn't about the hard foul she committed.

So what exactly did she mean by "White privilege"?

Unfortunately, despite plenty of social media posts since, she has never explained. Rather, she has maintained that she is a target of racism without providing any proof.

Therefore, we ought not take her complaint about the fan seriously unless there's video of him conducting himself inappropriately.

EX-ESPN HOST SAYS SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM DESERVED TO BE EJECTED AND PUNISHED — NOT DIJONAI CARRINGTON, WHO CLOTHESLINED HER

Chicago Sky guard DiJonai Carrington commits a flagrant 2 foul against Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham. (Kamil Krzaczynski/Imagn Images)

Even if/when Carrington reveals what she told officials the fan allegedly shouted at her, we cannot take her word for it. These are the consequences of her behavior. People stop believing you.

Apparently, that includes officials, who let the fan return to his seat after determining Carrington's complaint was "unfounded."

Likewise, we can no longer take Angel Reese seriously when she cries racism, given the similarly unfounded nature of her many accusations against fans.

DiJonai Carrington of the Chicago Sky fouls Sophie Cunningham of the Indiana Fever during the first half Aug. 8, 2026, at the United Center in Chicago, Ill. (Icon Sportswire via Getty Images)

For those who can't figure out why Sophie Cunningham and Caitlin Clark are so much more popular than other WNBA players, this is part of the reason why. Cunningham and Clark conduct themselves like professionals. They are likeable.

Conversely, players like Carrington act like entitled, dishonest wannabe victims.

articles.title: The scammer at your doctor's office may already know who you are
articles.excerpt:
Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.

You arrive at your doctor’s office and see a sign asking you to scan a QR code to check in. Later, you receive a text ...
articles.body_text:
Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.

You arrive at your doctor’s office and see a sign asking you to scan a QR code to check in. Later, you receive a text about a prescription. A Medicare notice with your name and address arrives in the mail. Before you leave, another QR code asks you to pay for parking. All of it looks routine. That’s exactly what can make these scams so dangerous. Criminals aren’t limited to sending obvious phishing messages to random people. Personal information available through data brokers and people-search websites can help scammers create medical, Medicare and payment scams that look like they were meant specifically for you.

Then a QR code gives them an easy way to send you to a convincing fake website asking for your Medicare number, patient portal login, credit card information or other sensitive data. Here’s what to watch for during your next trip to the doctor’s office and one important step that can make you harder for scammers to target in the first place.

New! Free live CyberGuy class: Protect Your Money From Today’s Biggest Threats

Join us Saturday, Aug. 29, at 10 a.m. ET for a free CyberGuy LIVE class covering five simple steps to help defend yourself against AI scams, fraud, identity theft and financial hacks. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson will explain how to set up bank alerts, strengthen your account logins, protect your phone number, freeze your credit and help secure your retirement savings against unauthorized transfers. No technical experience is needed. You'll also receive our financial protection checklist, and every registrant will get a link to the class recording afterward.

Reserve your free spot today at CyberGuyLive.com.

META MEDICARE SCAM ADS TARGETING SENIORS FACE SCRUTINY

Scammers can use exposed personal data and fake QR codes to make medical, Medicare and payment schemes look legitimate. (iStock)

QR codes have become a normal part of healthcare. Doctors’ offices use them for check-in forms. Pharmacies use them for pickup information. Medicare Advantage and Part D plans may include them in enrollment materials and other communications. Hospitals and medical buildings increasingly use QR codes for parking payments. That familiarity works in a scammer’s favor. When you’re standing inside your doctor’s office, holding paperwork that looks official or looking at a sign next to a parking machine, you naturally expect the information to be legitimate. Scammers know that.

A QR code also hides something that a normal web link does not: where it is actually taking you. You can usually glance at a link in an email before clicking it. With a QR code, you see a square filled with black and white patterns. You don’t know where it leads until your phone reads it. That makes the location of the QR code itself part of the deception.

The mechanics of the scam are surprisingly simple.

Scan the code, and you may land on a website designed to resemble your insurer, pharmacy, doctor’s portal or payment processor.

QR code phishing is sometimes called "quishing." The challenge is that many people have become so accustomed to QR codes that scanning one no longer feels like clicking a link.

This is where these scams can become much more convincing. A criminal contacting you may already have access to details such as your:

Some of that information can appear on data broker and people-search websites. Think about the difference between receiving a generic message that says: "Your health coverage has changed." and receiving a notice addressed to you by name, sent to your correct home address and written to resemble something connected to Medicare or your health coverage. The second message feels far more believable. That’s why protecting yourself isn’t only about spotting a fake QR code. It's also about reducing the amount of personal information strangers can easily find about you online.

A QR code at a doctor’s office, pharmacy or hospital parking machine can send users to a fake website designed to steal sensitive information. (iStock)

These examples show how fraudulent QR codes can blend into places where people already expect to see them.

One Medicare beneficiary described receiving a letter that appeared to come from a major insurer and directed the recipient to scan a QR code to read an Annual Notice of Change. The letter reportedly closely resembled legitimate plan correspondence, but the QR code pointed to a shortened, lookalike web address instead of the insurer’s actual domain. This particular example is a reported account rather than a confirmed investigated incident, but it follows a familiar scam pattern: make an official-looking Medicare communication feel urgent and legitimate, then direct the victim somewhere controlled by the scammer.

At Totnes Community Hospital in the U.K., a fraudulent QR code sticker was discovered on a parking payment machine. One visitor who scanned the code to pay reportedly had £146.79 taken from her account. The scammers then attempted to take another £849 before her bank’s fraud team intervened. The hospital trust confirmed the fraudulent code and began monitoring payment machines at other locations.

Law enforcement in Redondo Beach and San Clemente, California, has documented scammers placing counterfeit QR code stickers next to legitimate parking payment instructions. A medical office or hospital parking structure can be an especially convincing place for this trick because people already expect to scan something to pay.

Older Americans frequently interact with healthcare systems, pharmacies, insurance providers and Medicare.

That means a message about a doctor's appointment, prescription pickup, Medicare coverage, insurance changes, medical paperwork or hospital parking may not seem unusual. Add accurate personal information to the message, and the scam can become even harder to recognize. That’s the real danger. The QR code might be the thing you scan, but the personal details surrounding it are what can make you trust it.

A few quick checks can help you determine whether a QR code deserves your trust.

Most modern phones display the destination before opening a QR code link. Look carefully at the web address. If the domain is unfamiliar, shortened, misspelled or slightly different from the organization’s normal website, don't continue.

If a receptionist, sign or piece of paperwork tells you to scan a QR code, there's nothing wrong with asking: "Is this your official QR code?" That simple question can protect you if someone has placed a fraudulent sticker over a legitimate code.

Before scanning a QR code on a sign, parking meter or payment machine, look closely. Be suspicious if the code:

An official-looking envelope does not guarantee that what’s inside is legitimate. If a Medicare or insurance notice tells you to scan a QR code, consider going directly to the organization’s known website instead. You can also call the phone number printed on your insurance card rather than relying on contact information supplied in an unexpected mailing.

FCC ROBOCALL CRACKDOWN COULD CHANGE PHONE PRIVACY

Patients can reduce their risk by checking QR code destinations, watching for tampering and limiting personal information available through data brokers. (iStock)

Whenever possible, use your healthcare provider’s official app or type its known website address directly into your browser. The same rule applies to Medicare, pharmacies and insurers. Don’t trust a QR code simply because it appears in a place you trust.

Enable two-factor authentication (2FA) for accounts that support it, especially:

Two-factor authentication adds another barrier even if a scammer manages to obtain your password.

Install operating system, browser and security updates when they become available. Updates can help protect against dangerous websites, malicious downloads and other threats you might encounter after scanning a fraudulent code.

If you see a QR code at a doctor’s office, hospital, pharmacy or parking facility that appears suspicious, tell an employee. Removing one fraudulent sticker could prevent many other people from scanning it. You can also report suspected fraud to the Federal Trade Commission at ReportFraud.ftc.gov.

Spotting a fraudulent QR code can protect you from one scam. Reducing the personal information available about you can make it harder for scammers to build convincing attacks in the first place. Data brokers and people-search websites can expose information such as your name, address, phone number, age range and household details. Those pieces of information may seem harmless on their own. Put together, they can give a criminal enough background information to make a Medicare notice, medical message or other scam feel surprisingly personal.

You can contact data brokers and people-search sites yourself and request that your information be removed. The challenge is that your information may appear across many different sites and can sometimes return after it has been removed.

A personal data removal service can help automate that process by sending removal requests to data brokers on your behalf and continuing to check whether your information reappears. No service can guarantee that every piece of personal information will disappear from the internet, but reducing what is easily available can give scammers fewer details to work with when trying to create a convincing, personalized attack.

Whether you handle removals yourself or use a service, periodically search for your name, phone number and address online to see what strangers can find. The less information that is readily available about you, the harder it can be for a scammer to make a fake medical message, Medicare notice or payment request look legitimate.

Check out my top picks for data removal services and get a free scan to find out if your personal information is already out on the web by visiting CyberGuy.com.

The most convincing scams don’t always feel random. They may include your name, address or other accurate personal details that make a fake medical notice, Medicare communication or payment request feel legitimate. A QR code at your doctor’s office, in a healthcare mailing or on a hospital parking machine can simply be the final step that sends you to a fraudulent website. Before scanning, check the destination, look for signs of tampering and confirm unfamiliar codes with staff. Whenever possible, go directly to the organization’s official website or app. Just as importantly, find out how much personal information about you is publicly available online. The less information scammers can easily find about you, the harder it becomes for them to create a scam that feels like it was made specifically for you.

Have you ever been asked to scan a QR code at a doctor’s office or pharmacy and wondered whether it was legitimate? Let us know by writing to us at Cyberguy.com
