articles.title: Three states prepare to execute killers Thursday in same-day event not seen since 2010
articles.excerpt: Nancy Grace, host of 'Crime Stories with Nancy Grace,' speaks with Sean Hannity about Bryan Kohberger's petition to reopen the Idaho college killings case. Grace passionately argues against Kohberger'...
articles.body_text:
Nancy Grace, host of 'Crime Stories with Nancy Grace,' speaks with Sean Hannity about Bryan Kohberger's petition to reopen the Idaho college killings case. Grace passionately argues against Kohberger's claim of innocence, citing his DNA found on the murder weapon sheath and his prior guilty plea.

Three men in three different states are scheduled to be executed by lethal injection on Thursday in an unusual same-day cluster of executions across the U.S.

Tennessee is set to execute Anthony Darrell Hines for the murder of a motel maid, while Alabama plans to put Jeremy Williams to death for raping and killing a 5-year-old girl after paying her mother $2,500 to let the child perform a sexual act. Oklahoma is also scheduled to execute Carlos Cuesta-Rodriguez for killing his girlfriend.

The Associated Press reported that three states last carried out executions on a single day on Jan. 7, 2010, when prisoners were put to death in Louisiana, Ohio and Texas.

TWO FLORIDA INMATES DIE IN RARE DOUBLE EXECUTION AFTER SCOTUS DENIES STAYS

Three executions were also set to happen on the same day in 2018, though only one took place after Alabama officials struggled to place an IV line and Texas granted a reprieve.

In this photo released 02 February by the Texas Department of Corrections, is the gurney used to execute prisoners by lethal injection; called the Death Chamber, the gurney is housed in the Huntsville Unit in Huntsville, Texas. (Texas Department of Corrections//AFP via Getty Images)

Florida executed two men in one day in July, bringing its total number of executions since the beginning of 2025 to 31.

Eleven states carried out executions last year. If Tennessee and Alabama proceed Thursday, six states will have put prisoners to death in 2026.

Hines, 66, is set to die for the 1985 killing of Catherine Jean Jenkins, a 54-year-old motel maid in Kingston Springs. Prosecutors said Hines stabbed Jenkins while she was at work.

JUDGE BLOCKS ALABAMAS NITROGEN GAS EXECUTION METHOD, RUES IT IS UNCONSTITUTIONALLY CRUEL

Tennessee death row inmate Anthony Darrell Hines is scheduled to be executed Thursday for the 1985 killing of motel maid Catherine Jean Jenkins. (TDOC Communications via AP)

He was first sentenced to death in 1986, won a new sentencing hearing on appeal and was sentenced to death again in 1989.

His execution is scheduled three months after Tennessee stopped another inmate’s lethal injection when officials could not establish an IV line.

Hines has asked the governor and the courts to intervene, arguing that the doctor involved in the May procedure was unqualified and could cause the same problems during his execution. He also said muscular atrophy and weight loss after two strokes could make it difficult to place an IV.

Officials were able to establish Tony Carruthers’ first IV line quickly during the May attempt. But they spent more than an hour trying to place a second line, his lawyer said after witnessing the procedure. The team tried Carruthers’ arm, hand and foot before moving to a central line.

ALABAMA DEATH ROW INMATE INSISTS INNOCENCE, URGES GOVERNOR TO MEET HIM BEFORE NITROGEN-GAS EXECUTION

Lee stopped Carruthers’ execution and delayed it for a year. Tennessee has not said whether the doctor involved in that procedure will participate in Hines’ execution.

Alabama death row inmate Jeremy Williams is scheduled to be executed Thursday for the 2021 rape and murder of 5-year-old Kamarie Holland. (Russell County Sheriff's Office)

In Alabama, Williams is set to be executed for the 2021 rape and murder of 5-year-old Kamarie Holland of Georgia.

Williams pleaded guilty, gave up his appeals and asked to be put to death.

Prosecutors said the 42-year-old paid Holland’s mother $2,500 before sexually assaulting and strangling the girl. They said he recorded the attack and kept her body so he could continue abusing it.

"To see on video what he did to this baby, what a grown man could do to a child, it’s shocking, it’s horrible, it’s disgusting," Russell County District Attorney Richard Chancey said. "It’s just a level of evil."

Williams was also investigated in Alaska in 2005 in connection with his infant daughter’s death, though no charges were filed until 2022.

Alabama has not carried out an execution this year. If Williams is put to death, he would be the first. A federal judge halted a planned nitrogen gas execution in the state back in June after finding the method unconstitutional.

SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST TRUE CRIME NEWS

Oklahoma death row inmate Carlos Cuesta-Rodriguez is scheduled to be executed Thursday for the 2003 killing of his girlfriend, Olimpia Fisher. (Oklahoma Department of Corrections via AP)

Oklahoma is also scheduled to execute Cuesta-Rodriguez on Thursday for the 2003 murder of his girlfriend, Olimpia Fisher, at their Oklahoma City home.

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE

Cuesta-Rodriguez has expressed regret over Fisher’s death but did not ask for clemency.

Fisher was preparing to leave Cuesta-Rodriguez when he shot her through one eye. He left her to scream for help for about eight minutes, then shot her through the other eye, killing her.

"He made her suffer because she dared to live beyond his control," Oklahoma Attorney General Gentner Drummond told the state’s Pardon and Parole Board on July 14.

LISTEN TO THE NEW 'CRIME & JUSTICE WITH DONNA ROTUNNO' PODCAST

The board rejected clemency in a 3-1 vote last month. Cuesta-Rodriguez’s lawyers had urged the board to let him remain in prison for life, pointing to his difficult childhood in Cuba, brain damage, post-traumatic stress disorder and major depression.

If Oklahoma carries out the execution, Cuesta-Rodriguez would be the state’s third execution this year and the 20th under Republican Gov. Kevin Stitt.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

Greg Wehner is a reporter for Fox News Digital covering U.S. news and crime, with a focus on breaking developments, law enforcement, public safety and major stories shaping communities across the country.

articles.title: Man who carried Clinton nuclear 'football' reveals what 'scares the hell out of me' about Air Force One story
articles.excerpt: Retired U.S. Air Force Lt. Col. Buzz Patterson says decoy operations are "there for a reason" — and exposing how they work could endanger President Donald Trump, future presidents, crews protecting th...
articles.body_text:
Retired U.S. Air Force Lt. Col. Buzz Patterson says decoy operations are "there for a reason" — and exposing how they work could endanger President Donald Trump, future presidents, crews protecting them and the press.

A retired Air Force lieutenant colonel who carried the nuclear "football" for former President Bill Clinton says the extraordinary Air Force One shell game departing Ankara, Turkey last month to protect President Donald Trump from a potential attack was hardly unprecedented.

"It was brilliant," retired Lt. Col. Robert "Buzz" Patterson told Fox News Digital. "I wish I had been a part of it. That's how well done it was."

But Patterson is warning that exposing the vital national security secrets behind such operations could put presidents, military personnel and the White House press corps in danger for years to come.

Patterson served as Clinton's senior military aide for a period of two years and was responsible for the president’s emergency satchel, and in a 20-minute interview Wednesday, he explained how presidential decoys, aircraft swaps and other acts of deception are longstanding tools used to protect the commander in chief, his senior officials and the "privileged" Air Force One press corps.

TRUMP USED CATERING TRUCK, AIR FORCE ONE DECOY TO EVADE IRAN THREAT: REPORT

What alarms him, Patterson said, is not that Trump’s security team used the tactic – including the catering truck sleight of hand he was intimately a part of during the Clinton administration – but that details of how it was done are now spilling into public view.

"I hope that they prosecute this to the fullest," Patterson said. "Whoever leaked that, in my opinion, and having been involved in this, was highly placed in that process."

"There’s only a few people who actually know exactly what’s going down, and that’s by design," he added. "So if somebody leaked it, it was somebody involved in the process, and that scares the hell out of me."

'DECOY' AIR FORCE ONE WAS PROTECTED BY US FIGHTER JETS, OFFICIAL SAYS

President Donald Trump boards the new Qatari-gifted Air Force One at RAF Mildenhall in Suffolk, Britain, after attending a NATO leaders summit in Turkey, on July 8, 2026. (Jonathan Ernst/Reuters)

His warning comes as Fox News reported Wednesday that the legacy presidential 747 used as a decoy after Trump secretly switched planes in Ankara, Turkey, last month was not sent into the sky unprotected.

A senior Trump administration official told Fox News that U.S. fighter jets protected the aircraft on its flight to the United Kingdom. Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent were also aboard with members of the traveling press corps, according to the official. Reporters had been instructed to keep their window shades closed.

Patterson said the fighter escort was exactly the sort of protection he would expect in a high-threat environment.

TRUMP SAYS HE'S IRAN'S 'NO. 1' TARGET AS RENEWED CONFLICT RAISES ASSASSINATION FEARS

President Donald Trump speaks to reporters in the press cabin of the new, Qatari-gifted Air Force One after changing planes to return to Washington from RAF Mildenhall, Britain, July 8, 2026. (Jonathan Ernst/Reuters)

"Yes, especially into war zones," Patterson said, when asked whether presidential aircraft are customarily escorted by fighter jets in such circumstances.

"We damn sure always do when we’re going to a theater of high threat," he said. "We did it with President Clinton in ’97. And we did it with Trump just a couple weeks ago, and we’ll do it with whoever the next president is."

TRUMP’S SLY PLANE SWITCH RAISES EYEBROWS OVER SAFETY OF PASSENGERS LEFT BEHIND ON BOARD

Trump’s July 8 departure from the NATO summit in Ankara involved a carefully staged deception.

Trump publicly boarded the familiar blue-and-white presidential 747 before being moved out of sight in an airport catering vehicle and transferred to a smaller Air Force C-32A. The legacy 747 then departed for Britain while Trump traveled separately. He later reunited with the presidential aircraft in the United Kingdom before continuing his journey aboard the newer, Qatari-donated 747.

Trump said Tuesday that he was following the direction of the Secret Service and military.

Patterson said the broader concept of confusing potential attackers about the president’s movements is routine.

WHITE HOUSE PUSHED FOR PROTOCOL TO PRESERVE CORRESPONDENTS' CREDIBILITY AFTER TRUMP'S SECRET PLANE SWITCH

President Donald Trump greets security forces members at RAF Mildenhall in Suffolk, Britain, after arriving to switch to the Qatari-gifted Air Force One following his participation in a NATO leaders summit in Turkey, July 8, 2026. (Jonathan Ernst/Reuters)

"We use decoys all the time," he said. "We use decoy in the motorcade routes."

"You'll sometimes see the two beasts will switch out under bridges and overpasses. We do the same thing with airplanes, especially in international trips. There's always two Air Force ones that go. Obviously one's a decoy and it's also a spare for spare parts in case something happens to the primary.

"It works," he added, "and for people to want to have visibility into actually how it works would be particularly troubling and it would cause reverberations in our American system for years."

SECRET SERVICE AGENT ON JD VANCE'S DETAIL INVESTIGATED FOR ALLEGEDLY LEAKING OPERATIONAL SECURITY INFO

That is why, he argued, demands to expose the mechanics of the latest operation risk doing more damage than the public scrutiny is worth.

Patterson said the protections are intended not merely for Trump, Clinton or any individual president, but to ensure continuity of the presidency itself.

"President Trump's only got two more years," he said. "These programs are going to be in place for the foreseeable future, and they've been in place in our past for quite a while. So it's not just about Trump. These programs exist to protect no matter who the president is and the team around him."

Patterson, who is a conservative and outspoken New York Times bestselling author highly critical of the man he carried the nuclear football for, warned divisive politics against Trump is dangerous for U.S. national security.

TWO YEARS AFTER BUTLER, THREATS AGAINST TRUMP KEEP ASSASSINATION ATTEMPT IN SHARP FOCUS

"Like I was with President Clinton – I wasn't a huge President Clinton fan but they hired me into that position, the White House did – and I swore an oath to the office of the presidency, and I did it," Patterson said. "And I think that the people that are working for President Trump right now, whether they like him or don't like him, or agree with his politics or don't agree with this politics, they have to understand that we're there – the Secret Service guys, the apparatus is there – to protect the human being and the office."

Patterson also revealed that Trump was not the first president he knew of to use an airport catering vehicle as part of a clandestine movement: "As far as I know, President Clinton was the first one to do it."

Decades before Trump was moved between aircraft in Ankara, Patterson said a catering truck was used to discreetly move Clinton aboard a presidential aircraft during an episode that was never publicly reported at the time.

"I won't go into a lot of detail, but, President Clinton was incapable of going up the front steps," he said. "So we used a catering truck to get them onto the back of the airplane, unbeknownst to anybody else that was there except for a few of us. And we never told anybody and nobody ever reported it."

TRUMP HAS BECOME AMERICA'S MOST TARGETED LEADER, FACING THREATS EVERY FEW MONTHS

"And we flew back to DC kind of unannounced. And we've done it before. I was on with President Clinton in 1997 when we did the surprise visit to Bosnia. So he went to Bosnia on Christmas Eve to surprise the troops. So we didn't tell anybody then. I was all on that trip the entire way, 36 hours nonstop that day. And we didn't tell anybody, and the press didn't know, and they never complained about it.

"And it was important. We wanted to get President Clinton into a war zone without anybody else knowing about it. And that's kind of what was happening to Trump. They wanted to him out of a potential war zone, without anybody knowing about it.

"We do it all the time. It's safe, it's reliable, and the public does not need to know."

Past presidents have repeatedly used secrecy and deception for travel into dangerous areas. Clinton used decoy aircraft during a 2000 trip to Pakistan, while subsequent presidents have made covert or tightly held trips to Iraq, Afghanistan and Ukraine. The precise circumstances and level of knowledge afforded to traveling reporters have differed between administrations.

Patterson pushed back against criticism that Trump’s operation improperly endangered the reporters and officials who continued aboard the legacy presidential aircraft.

He noted that the aircraft was carrying not only journalists but an Air Force crew and senior government officials — and, as Fox News has now reported, was protected by fighter aircraft.

"We’re not going to put those people at risk either," Patterson said flatly of the Air Force personnel.

He argued that some of the media criticism has lost sight of the wider security apparatus involved in presidential travel.

"A lot of what is being spouted on social media and in our mainstream media is factually incorrect," Patterson said, "and it’s actually troubling because it’s going to endanger not only President Trump, but future presidents to come."

Patterson called efforts to expose the procedures "incredibly dangerous" and "irresponsible."

The danger, he said, extends beyond the president.

"It endangers everybody in the process — Secret Service guys, military aide guys, Air Force guys that are on alert, Army guys that are on alert," Patterson said.

The retired officer said presidential protection plans are deliberately compartmentalized so that very few people know the full operation.

That is what makes the source of the disclosures particularly concerning to him.

This photo shows the press boarding the Air Force One aircraft from Ankara, while a catering truck is located at the front of the plane. (Pool)

Patterson warned there could also be a longer-term cost to revealing too much about presidential deception tactics: Future commanders in chief could lose the ability to make surprise visits to troops or enter high-threat regions at all.

If the tactics become predictable, he argued, planners would have to devise entirely new security procedures.

"If we were to expose everything, we would have to overhaul the entire security apparatus of the United States of America," Patterson said, warning that doing so could put "the presidency and the Cabinet members in incredible danger."

Asked whether overexposing such programs could effectively prevent Trump or future presidents from making some high-risk overseas trips, Patterson agreed.

For Patterson, that makes the argument over the Trump flight bigger than one president, one press corps or one flight out of Turkey.

The tactics being publicly dissected today, he warned, may be the same ones needed to save a future president — and everyone traveling with that president — tomorrow.

"We just need to leave them alone," Patterson said.

Eric Mack is a breaking news reporter and writer Sunday through Thursday, 6 a.m. ET to 2 p.m. ET, with a particular interest in stories that lead the news cycle on politics, elections, foreign affairs and government.

articles.title: BZZR 'cutting out the noise' from sports social media space great for creators, sportscaster Jon Alba says
articles.excerpt:
Sportscaster Jon Alba talks to Fox News Digital about the importance of BZZR in the sports social media space.

If you fire off the wrong hot take, you could subject yourself to endless notifications ...
articles.body_text:
Sportscaster Jon Alba talks to Fox News Digital about the importance of BZZR in the sports social media space.

If you fire off the wrong hot take, you could subject yourself to endless notifications for messages that might make you lose some sleep. BZZR, a social media platform dedicated solely to sports content, is hoping to change that.

COMPLETE PRO WRESTLING COVERAGE ON FOX NEWS DIGITAL

Jon Alba is a content creator with BZZR. (BZZR)

Jon Alba, an Emmy Award-winning sportscaster who co-hosts "The Extreme Life of Matt Hardy" with the legendary professional wrestler, told Fox News Digital he believed that there was a space missing for sports fans to connect online without the hate and vitriol. He said it’s what makes BZZR the place to be for those who have cemented themselves as reputable content creators and those looking to get reps in.

"I have always felt like there was a spot in the sports media space that was unoccupied where a virtual sports bar could meet people who wanted to engage in that space specifically," he said. "When I was 15 years old, back in the early days of podcasting, podcasting didn't even exist. It was like online sports talk radio. There was a platform called YouCaster and it was essentially a bunch of sports fans, wannabe sports broadcasters, creating content and congregating around each other's content. And the platform didn't last very long, but it was such a great idea.

"And now in the age of access for all of these creators to have a space that is dedicated to solely creating instantaneous, engaging sports content and cutting out the noise, I think that's awesome for the space and it's a great way for anyone to get an opportunity to get reps and get better at creating content in the sports space. So, I think it's a great arena for that."

BZZR has made it a point to block out the noise and stick solely to sports and it’s what drew Alba to the platform. The social media platform has partnered with the Texas Rangers, John Bradshaw Layfield, MVP, Dwayne Swayze and Kayla Becker – to name a few.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

MVP, Dwayne Swayze and Kayla Becker have all partnered with the sports-focused social media platform BZZR. (BZZR)

"There's so much trash out there today, whether it's AI garbage or engagement bait, rage bait, where people just say things for the sake of saying things, and it's been one of my least favorite evolutions of the sports media space in the last decade where people who want to make noise get rewarded for doing so without any substance to what they're saying," he said. "And I think the advantage of a place like BZZR is that you have people on the platform who are there for the right reason, who want to create good, engaging content that furthers conversation that gets them better at creating sports content and creates a space that people actually want to talk about sports in, as silly as it sounds.

"I don't think we have that many of them right now that do so in a way that has integrity and is genuinely fun to sort through. So that's why I've really gone behind the idea of BZZR and I think it's cool to see that it has grown in a short period of time."

Hardy agreed that the concept of having a place solely for sports was a good idea.

Texas Rangers fans are seen with large claws during Game 3 of the 2010 World Series against the San Francisco Giants at Rangers Ballpark on Saturday, Oct. 30, 2010, in Arlington, Texas. (MLB via Getty Images)

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

"The best thing about social media is it gives everyone a voice. The worst thing about social media is it gives everyone a voice and that very much holds true," Hardy added.

Hardy and Alba’s podcast drops every Friday morning as they look back at Hardy’s career and swap stories about some of the most important moments in pro wrestling history.

Ryan Gaydos is a senior editor for Fox News Digital.

articles.title: DAVID MARCUS: Why it's too late for Dems to ditch Piker and his America-hating socialism
articles.excerpt: Far-left streamer Hasan Piker reacted to Francesca Hong’s loss in Wisconsin’s Democratic gubernatorial primary by warning that the Democratic establishment will no longer underestimate the socialist l...
articles.body_text:
Far-left streamer Hasan Piker reacted to Francesca Hong’s loss in Wisconsin’s Democratic gubernatorial primary by warning that the Democratic establishment will no longer underestimate the socialist left and that "the knives will be out."

Democrats scored a narrow, but ultimately pyrrhic, victory in Wisconsin Tuesday night, as the wacky Thanksgiving-hating and Hasan Piker-backed gubernatorial candidate Francesca Hong lost the primary to a more moderate candidate. But their socialism problem is far from cured.

Just as in Michigan two weeks ago, the polls in this Democratic primary reflected about as much reality as Alice in Wonderland, as all of them had Hong with a seemingly insurmountable lead of over 15 points.

The prediction markets had Hong’s chances of winning at 96% on Tuesday morning, but something happened on the way to her coronation. Actual flesh-and-blood voters decided that socialist policies such as abolishing police and ICE aren’t really what they want.

DEMOCRAT ESTABLISHMENT STRIKES BACK AS SOCIALIST CANDIDATE DOWNED IN BATTLEGROUND PRIMARY

This column, based on reporting from the ground in the Midwest, has been warning for weeks that the polls have been absurdly favoring socialist candidates such as Adbul El-Sayed in Michigan’s Senate primary who squeaked out a 1-point win after every survey put him up double digits.

RNC national spokesperson Natalie Baldassarre called on Democrats to disavow Piker after he blamed the Democratic establishment for undermining the socialist left. (Jamie Vera/Fox News)

This has left Democrats with the most serious problem they have faced in a generation, because half of their voters seem to want a socialist utopia while the other half just wants a normal, everyday Democratic candidate, to the extent those still even exist.

Democratic establishment leaders like Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer and House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries keep insisting that the Democrats just have a big tent, and that this is a good thing. But what does that really mean?

If the Democrats' "big tent" includes proposals such as abolishing the Senate and Supreme Court, seizing private property and, as one of New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani’s top aides put it, "impoverishing the White middle class," then voters have a right to believe that electing Democrats might bring those things about.

JONATHAN TURLEY: NOTHING SAYS 'BIG TENT' LIKE A GOOD COMMUNIST POGROM

In the final 10 days of the Michigan race, Piker and the DSA were basically El-Sayed’s running mates. At first, the party thought it had found electoral gold as the fabulist polls posited a socialist supercharged blowout.

They were ready to send Piker everywhere and to plaster his face all over America.

When that lead turned out to be fool's gold, Democrats realized they had made a huge mistake, and that Piker and his lunatic ravings about Israel and murdering United States senators had done far more harm than good.

Even having realized that, however, the party is stuck with Piker and the DSA now. For weeks, Democrats have been insisting that the antisemitic Twitch streamer is a major voice for youth who must be given space and a platform, and that America is trending towards socialism.

HASAN PIKER CALLS FOR DEMOCRATS WHO OPPOSE ABDUL EL-SAYED TO BE 'PUNISHED'

It is far too late for Democrats to disavow Piker now, and the odds of him shutting up and going away on his own, especially after last week’s Rolling Stone fashion shoot, are somewhere between narrow and non-existent.

Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed speaks after a radio appearance at Dr. Horace Sheffield's GOTV Community Rally on Aug. 1, 2026, in Detroit, Mich. El-Sayed holds a 15-point lead against Rep. Haley Stevens (D-Mich.) according to a recent poll. (Getty Images)

Piker is to Republicans what cowbell is to Christopher Walken: They need more, the GOP has a fever and the only cure is more Hasan Piker, who seems to say things daily that make Democrats miss nutty Graham Platner.

Republicans are going to tie El-Sayed and every Democratic candidate in America to Piker and communist crazies, and where is the lie? Who in their party other than Sen. John Fetterman, D-Pa., has said a word against them?

BLAKEMAN CUTS INTO HOCHUL'S NEW YORK GOVERNOR'S RACE LEAD IN NEW POLL, AS LIKELY VOTERS GIVE DSA JUDGMENT

When you combine this with the galaxy-sized polling misses, all in favor of the left, in this cycle, who is to say that Michelle Tafoya can’t flip the Minnesota Senate seat red or that Bruce Blakeman can’t unseat Gov. Kathy Hochul in the Empire State’s governor's race?

Elections are stories, not math problems, and boy do Republicans have a good story to tell now that Democrats have embraced Piker and the radical left. If destroying the constitution and immiserating White people is inside the Democrat tent, there are a lot of ordinary, everyday American voters who will not be.

Democrats will try very hard in the coming weeks to move to the center and put all of this socialism behind them, but so long as they are tied to Piker and the communists, they will never be able to get there.

CLICK HERE TO READ MORE FROM DAVID MARCUS

David Marcus is a columnist living in West Virginia and the author of "Charade: The COVID Lies That Crushed A Nation."

articles.title: Beach hero jumps into the water after spotting 3 girls in danger of drowning
articles.excerpt:
UC Davis water polo player Lillie Vehling describes the moment she spotted three girls struggling in the water and jumped in to help, pulling them to safety one by one. (Source: KCPQ)

A California co...
articles.body_text:
UC Davis water polo player Lillie Vehling describes the moment she spotted three girls struggling in the water and jumped in to help, pulling them to safety one by one. (Source: KCPQ)

A California college student rescued three girls who were in danger of drowning at a Seattle park after spotting them struggling in the water during a festival.

The student, Lillie Vehling, is a Division I water polo player at the University of California, Davis, FOX 13 Seattle reported.

Vehling was in Seattle for Seafair, the city's annual summer festival, when she spotted three girls struggling in the waters of Lake Washington near Genesee Park on July 31.

EXTREME DEPTH MADE FATAL CAVE DIVE PERILOUS AT LUXURY HONEYMOON DESTINATION

A California native, Vehling had gone to Genesee Park to watch the U.S. Navy Blue Angels flight demonstration squadron.

The girls "did not look very good" in the water, Vehling said in an interview with FOX 13 Seattle.

UC Davis water polo player Lillie Vehling rescued three girls who had been struggling in Lake Washington during Seattle's annual Seafair festival. (FOX 13 Seattle)

"They were already bobbing up and down, trying to get breaths, and one of the girls was actually drowning the others in order to breathe," she said.

SHARK WEEK ADVISORY AS WARMING SEAS PUSH BLACKTIPS FARTHER NORTH ALONG EAST COAST

Vehling said that she saved the girl who was drowning the others first "so that the others weren't even in worse shape."

Fox News Digitial reached out to Vehling for more details.

"I removed them one by one," she told FOX 13. "The first girl — I, again, don't really remember how I did it, but I got her back to the shallow water."

After rescuing the second swimmer, Vehling untangled the third girl from the buoy rope and brought her up to safety.

CARIBBEAN HOT SPOT GRIPPED BY WATER CRISIS, AND TOURISTS SCRAMBLE TO RESCHEDULE PLANS

"Unfortunately, by the time I had gotten to the third girl, it was just the top of her head that was there," Vehling said.

"I just saw her black hair in the water barely floating and when I got to her, she was unconscious. I lifted her head up out of the water and had my arm underneath her armpit holding her up," she added.

Vehling had gone to Genesee Park to watch the U.S. Navy Blue Angels flight demonstration squadron when the emergency unfolded. (Al Drago/Getty Images)

The girl coughed up water and regained consciousness, according to FOX 13.

Seafair later honored Vehling for the rescue, inviting her to its gala — where she was knighted and named Seafair royalty.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

She was also given a special opportunity to see the U.S. Navy Blue Angels, a squadron she has long admired.

The California native noticed three girls bobbing up and down in Lake Washington (lake pictured above) and struggling to get breaths. (Genna Martin/San Francisco Chronicle via Getty Images)

Fox News Digital reached out to Seafair for comment.

Drowning is the leading cause of death among children ages 1 to 4 and the second-leading cause of unintentional injury death among children ages 5 to 14, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC).

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Similar rescues have made recent headlines across the country.

Seafair, Seattle's annual summer festival (pictured above), honored Lillie Vehling after she rescued three girls from drowning in Lake Washington. (Genna Martin/San Francisco Chronicle via Getty Images)

Earlier this summer, two Florida lifeguards were credited with saving a 5-year-old boy who was pulled unconscious from the ocean at Silver Beach after his frantic family flagged them down for help.

In LA County, lifeguards performed nearly 2,000 ocean rescues over a single weekend amid extreme heat and dangerous surf conditions.

Andrea Margolis is a lifestyle reporter for Fox News Digital and Fox Business. Readers can follow her on X at @andreamargs or send story tips to andrea.margolis@fox.com.

articles.title: French ambassador to CAR investigated over claims he hosted dozens of women
articles.excerpt:
Disciplinary proceedings under way after security concerns raised over reported visits to official residence

France has opened disciplinary proceedings against its ambassador to Central African Repub...
articles.body_text:
Disciplinary proceedings under way after security concerns raised over reported visits to official residence

France has opened disciplinary proceedings against its ambassador to Central African Republic over allegations of misconduct, after claims he brought dozens of women into his official residence, raising potential security concerns.

The investigation comes as Paris seeks to rebuild relations with CAR after their sharp deterioration in recent years amid Russia’s expanding influence in the former French colony.

The French weekly newspaper Le Canard enchaîné reported that the ambassador, Bruno Foucher, 65, brought about 30 women between the ages of 20 and 30 into his residence during the period of January 2024 to March 2026, with some of them staying overnight. The visits prompted officials to report a security breach.

The ambassador acknowledged having had sexual relations with two young women, the weekly said.

The French foreign ministry said: “At the initiative of the ministry, an administrative investigation was carried out in Bangui in 2026. Upon receipt of the findings of this mission, and at the request of the minister, the ministry initiated disciplinary proceedings against the ambassador. These proceedings are ongoing.”

The ministry conducted an on-site inspection in April, which led to the opening of disciplinary proceedings.

Foucher is a career diplomat who has served as ambassador to CAR since 2023. He was ambassador to Lebanon from 2017 to 2020, to Iran from 2011 to 2016, and to Chad between 2006 and 2011.

According to Le Canard enchaîné, which said it obtained the inspection report, the ambassador received about 15 visits a month.

He also allegedly instructed staff to allow one of the young women to stay at the residence during his absence.

Russia maintains a strong foothold in CAR, primarily through the Wagner paramilitary group, which plays a key role in providing security for the country’s president, Faustin-Archange Touadéra.

French officials have accused Russians of fostering anti-French sentiment in a number of African countries.

The French foreign minister, Jean-Noël Barrot, praised the “complete restoration of relations” between France and CAR when he visited Bangui in March.

articles.title: Ebola outbreak caused by new ‘animal transmission’: What that means
articles.excerpt: The Ebola outbreak currently ravaging the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) was caused by a new transmission from animals to humans rather than by variants linked to earlier outbreaks, according ...
articles.body_text:
The Ebola outbreak currently ravaging the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) was caused by a new transmission from animals to humans rather than by variants linked to earlier outbreaks, according to a new study published in the medical journal Nature Medicine.

The virus in eastern DRC has killed more than 2,000 people of 4,449 recorded cases, making it the fastest-moving Ebola outbreak on record. It was formally declared on May 15 , though genetic sequencing later revealed the virus had actually begun circulating in February.

On Wednesday, the World Health Organization (WHO) said the current Bundibugyo strain of the Ebola virus is spreading faster than health authorities can contain it and is on track to become the deadliest outbreak on record.

So what have scientists discovered about how it was transmitted to humans? And can it be contained?

In a report published this week in the medical journal Nature Medicine, researchers from the DRC, Uganda, Belgium and other countries analysed the genetic make-up of virus samples from 22 patients in the DRC and Uganda. They found that the outbreak strain was genetically distinct from previous Bundibugyo Ebola viruses seen in outbreaks in 2007 and 2012.

The report suggested that the virus began with a new animal-to-human transmission incident, which then spread to other people.

The animal source has not been specified but the researchers said the outbreak in Uganda was linked to the outbreak in the DRC.

Earlier, health officials in the region said the outbreak is being driven by the rare Bundibugyo strain of the virus, for which no vaccine has yet been developed.

Krutika Kuppalli, an infectious diseases doctor with experience in Ebola and outbreak response, explained that the study citing a “new animal transmission” as the reason for the outbreak, does not mean that a new form of Ebola has suddenly emerged or that animals are now transmitting the virus differently.

“What the genomic data suggest is that the current outbreak began with a new ‘zoonotic spillover’ event – meaning the virus likely crossed independently from an animal reservoir into a person – rather than resulting from continued circulation or re-emergence of virus from a previous human outbreak,” she said.

“After that initial spillover, the outbreak has been driven predominantly by human-to-human transmission,” she added.

On Wednesday, WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said that at its current pace, the current Ebola outbreak is on track to eclipse the West African outbreak of 2014 to 2016. That crisis killed at least 11,300 people of a reported 28,600 cases and accelerated the push to develop a vaccine.

That was a different strain of the Ebola virus known as Zaire and the vaccine developed then does not work for the current strain, which is spreading.

Dr Abdirahman Mahamud, WHO’s director for health emergency alert and response operations, said the agency’s moderate projection has the outbreak peaking within six months. Under a more severe scenario, it could stretch on for nine to 12 months.

“Beyond the zoonotic spillover event from animals to humans, it is the human-to-human transmission dynamics of the Bundibugyo virus that make it dangerous,” Kaja Abbas, associate professor of infectious disease epidemiology and dynamics at the London School of Hygiene & Tropical Medicine and Nagasaki University, told Al Jazeera.

Dr Kuppalli also emphasised that the way this strain of the virus was initially transmitted to humans does not make it intrinsically more dangerous.

Kuppalli said the animal origin of the virus does not change required treatment.

“Once someone develops Ebola disease, management is based on the virus causing the illness and the patient’s clinical condition, not whether their infection ultimately originated from an animal or from another person. What matters here is that Bundibugyo virus (BDBV) currently does not have the same licensed, proven virus-specific therapeutics that we have for Zaire ebolavirus,” she said.

“Supportive care, which includes aggressive fluid and electrolyte management, treatment of shock and organ dysfunction, and management of co-infections, remains critical, while investigational therapeutics are being evaluated,” she added.

“Ebola outbreaks have historically begun through zoonotic spillover. The bigger concern is what it tells us about our preparedness: we still do not fully understand where and when these spillover events will occur, making prevention and early detection extremely difficult.”

“In this outbreak, there also appears to have been substantial transmission before the outbreak was recognised, which gave the virus an opportunity to establish multiple chains of transmission,” she added.

Researchers who worked on the new study said increasing “decentralised laboratory diagnostics capacity, including genomic sequencing capacity and timely detection ” could help pre-empt future outbreaks.

Clinicians are also working to develop treatments.

“While no licensed treatments or vaccines exist today, experimental therapeutics and vaccines are in the clinical development pipeline that are specifically targeted towards the strains of the Bundibugyo virus currently circulating in the ongoing Ebola outbreak in the DRC and Uganda during 2026,” Abbas said.

While a vaccine against the latest strain is being developed, a WHO official said in May that medical supplies, including personal protective equipment (PPE) ⁠⁠to prevent Ebola, were being sent to ⁠⁠the DRC.

“We have sent 12 tonnes of supply. An additional six are arriving. These include personal protective equipment for ⁠⁠front-line health workers [and] samples,” Anne Ancia, WHO representative in the DRC’s Ituri province, told media in May.

At the forefront of the fight to break the spread in the DRC are health workers who have been treating patients while also dealing with the risk of becoming infected themselves.

More than 100 health workers have been infected and about 35 have died.

The response to the outbreak has been further complicated by several factors, including strikes by unpaid health workers, misinformation and cultural traditions. These have included open-casket family burials of some of those killed by the virus, potentially increasing the risk of further transmission.

Kuppalli said better Ebola preparedness is required, not just focusing on stopping transmission once an outbreak has been recognised.

“We also need much stronger health surveillance at the human-animal interface, broader diagnostics capable of detecting different Ebola viruses and medical countermeasures that work across Ebola species,” she said.

“This outbreak is showing us the consequences when the virus gets a several-month head start.”

Many countries have raised concerns about the latest Ebola virus outbreak and some, such as Bahrain, have suspended entry for 30 days for foreign travellers arriving from South Sudan, the DRC and Uganda.

Neighbouring countries, including Rwanda and Uganda, have introduced measures to prevent the virus from crossing their borders.

Rwanda imposed health restrictions, including barring entry to foreign travellers who had been in the DRC in the previous 30 days.

The US warned that travellers, including US citizens, who have been in the DRC within 21 days before departure will not be allowed to board commercial flights to US destinations.

Governments across Asia have also begun introducing border screening and bolstering quarantine preparedness.

articles.title: Lebanese Americans sue US over Israel’s rights abuses in Lebanon war
articles.excerpt: Dozens of Lebanese Americans have filed a class action civil lawsuit against the US government and several defence contractors, saying their role in Israel’s war in Lebanon is a violation of a US law ...
articles.body_text:
Dozens of Lebanese Americans have filed a class action civil lawsuit against the US government and several defence contractors, saying their role in Israel’s war in Lebanon is a violation of a US law that bars assistance to foreign governments known to be committing human rights abuses.

The lawsuit, filed on Tuesday in the US District Court in Michigan, names Secretary of State Marco Rubio, as well as Lockheed Martin, Boeing, and Caterpillar as defendants.

The plaintiffs are the Michigan-based Arab American Civil Rights League group and 16 individuals, all US citizens with property in Lebanon that has been impacted by what they claim is indiscriminate use of force by Israel during the war.

Plaintiffs include Nasser Beydoun, a prominent Michigan businessman and politician who alleges in the lawsuit that Israeli forces destroyed his family home in Bint Jbeil, southern Lebanon, “without any military necessity or justification”.

The lawsuit argues that by supplying Israel with funds and weapons used in this manner, the US government is in violation of the Leahy Law, which bars military assistance, training, or equipment to foreign militaries that are credibly linked to gross human rights violations.

Defence contractors selling equipment to Israel, the plaintiffs claim, similarly should be halted as the companies are knowingly helping the country commit illegal actions in the conflict.

“The law is very clear and has been enforced around the world, but when it comes to Israel, there is zero enforcement,” Nabih Ayad, a lawyer and the head of the Arab American Civil Rights League, said on Wednesday.

In the Lebanon conflict, Ayad said, “You have credible information about gross human rights violations that have happened…yet you are doing nothing about it.”

This June, US President Donald Trump acknowledged Israel’s indiscriminate use of force in Lebanon, saying, “You don’t have to knock down an apartment house every time you’re looking for somebody”.

The lawsuit is seeking to become a class action, representing what the plaintiffs say are tens of thousands of Lebanese Americans with property in Lebanon that has been damaged, or could later be damaged, by Israeli air strikes and other military activity.

The Arab American Civil Rights League has been involved in several major civil rights lawsuits in recent years, including a challenge against the previous Trump administration’s so-called “Muslim ban”, a lawsuit that sued major banks for discriminating against Muslim and Arab Americans, and a 2023 suit seeking to compel the US to help evacuate US citizens trapped in Gaza.

articles.title: Will Trump’s next press secretary be a better liar than the first five?
articles.excerpt:
As Karoline Leavitt plans to step down, it’s apparent how the president above all values a readiness to twist the truth

As Karoline Leavitt prepares to step down from her role as Donald Trump’s fifth...
articles.body_text:
As Karoline Leavitt plans to step down, it’s apparent how the president above all values a readiness to twist the truth

As Karoline Leavitt prepares to step down from her role as Donald Trump’s fifth White House press secretary, a brief review of her tenure, and that of her predecessors, makes clear that the most fabulist president in US history prizes one quality above all else in the women and men who speak for him: a willingness to tell outrageous lies.

Leavitt started her tenure by telling a wild falsehood at her very first news conference, when she claimed that the Biden administration had planned to use $50m in taxpayer dollars to send condoms to Gaza. Later the same day, the Guardian reported that the claim was directly contradicted by USAID records.

Sean Spicer, Trump’s first White House press secretary, also told perhaps his most blatant lie the first time he stepped behind the podium in the White House briefing room.

The day after Trump’s first inauguration in 2017, Spicer summoned reporters to the briefing room and relentlessly scolded them for not reporting the lie that “this was the largest audience to ever witness an inauguration – period – both in person and around the globe”. Visual evidence made it clear that this was untrue.

Four months later, his successor, Sarah Huckabee Sanders, insisted to reporters that FBI agents were privately delighted that Trump had fired James Comey, then the FBI director.

Asked by a reporter what she had based that on, Sanders replied: “I can speak to my own personal experience, I’ve heard from countless members of the FBI that are grateful and thankful for the president’s decision.”

Sanders later admitted to the special counsel investigating Russian interference in the 2016 election, an investigation Comey had started, that she had invented this claim. According to special counsel Robert Mueller’s report: “Sanders acknowledged to investigators that her comments were not founded on anything.”

Stephanie Grisham, whose nine-month tenure as press secretary was marked by her notable failure to hold even one formal press briefing, admitted in her memoir that she had lied for Trump, but she never acknowledged that her biggest lie was told before she even took up the role.

In 2018, when she still worked for Melania Trump, the president’s wife, Grisham insisted, in the face of concrete evidence to the contrary, that Trump was telling the truth when he claimed that he “predicted” the results of the 2016 Brexit referendum the day before the vote during a visit to Scotland.

In fact, as dozens of journalists on that trip confirmed, Trump had actually arrived in Scotland the morning after the vote, when the result was clear. Still Grisham doubled and tripled down on the lie to defend Trump’s claim, which he went on to make again and again in the following years.

Kayleigh McEnany, Trump’s fourth press secretary, routinely lied for the president throughout the Covid pandemic in 2020, but perhaps never more blatantly than when she was asked, at a June briefing that year, why the president kept using the racist term “kung flu” to refer to the coronavirus, which had emerged in China.

“The president doesn’t,” McEnany claimed, two days after he had clearly used that term at a rally in Oklahoma. “What the president does do,” she continued, “is point to the fact that the origin of the virus is China. It’s a fair thing to point out.”

The very next day, Trump used the racist term again, to great acclaim from his supporters, at a Turning Point USA rally in an Arizona megachurch.

articles.title: UNICEF Gaza findings ‘completely shatters’ starvation claims against Israel, State Dept says
articles.excerpt:
Danny Danon, Israeli UN envoy says new Gaza nutrition findings expose "fabricated" starvation claims.

The Trump State Department has reacted to a new report by UNICEF on malnutrition in Gaza by sayin...
articles.body_text:
Danny Danon, Israeli UN envoy says new Gaza nutrition findings expose "fabricated" starvation claims.

The Trump State Department has reacted to a new report by UNICEF on malnutrition in Gaza by saying it "completely shatters" the allegations that Israel deliberately starved civilians in the Hamas-run enclave.

The outcry of criticism comes as a report used by the United Nations and quoted by much of the world's media projected starvation in Gaza well into June.

Following Hamas’ invasion of southern Israel on Oct 7, 2023, that led to the deaths of some 1,200 people and the kidnapping of 251 Israeli and foreign nationals, the Jewish state invaded Gaza, which led to accusations of genocide and deliberate starvation tactics used against Gazans.

The UNICEF-led National Nutrition Cluster report from last month was able to reach 1,335 children under age 5 throughout 83% of the Gaza Strip to assess its risk of malnutrition. Malnutrition rates were determined by weight-for-height Z-score (WHZ) and mid-upper-arm circumference (MUAC). Using WHZ figures, rates ranged from 0.2% in Khan Younis and Rafah to 0.8% in Gaza City. MUAC measurements found malnutrition rates ranging from 1.5% in Gaza City to 1.9% in Deir Al-Balah.

About 17% of the population could not be surveyed due to security and operational constraints.

TRUMP ADMINISTRATION PROBES UNRWA OVER ALLEGED EMPLOYMENT OF 1,500 TERRORISTS

Palestinians in Gaza carry supplies dropped by Jordan and UAE air forces on July. 27 (TPS-IL)

A State Department spokesperson told Fox News Digital that "UNICEF’s latest findings demonstrate another example that completely shatters the countless false allegations against Israel of deliberate starvation of civilians in Gaza. There are U.N. entities, media outlets and NGOs that should retract and correct their politicized and baseless attacks on Israel – which has provided an unprecedented over 2 million tons of food into Gaza since the ceasefire."

The rates of malnutrition UNICEF documented are on par with, or substantially lower than, those in some neighboring countries. According to a post on X from the Israeli Coordinator of Government Activities in the Territories (COGAT), acute malnutrition figures in the region range from 1.3% in Gaza, Lebanon, and Turkey to 2.3% in Jordan, 3.3% in Egypt, 12.2% in Syria, and 17.7% in Sudan.

UNICEF’s report has raised ire from onlookers who took issue with the Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC) statement that famine was "confirmed" in Gaza in August 2025.

The catalyst for the uproar was the IPC's warning from August 2025 that famine had reached Gaza Governorate. At that time, the IPC estimated that 'through June 2026, at least 132,000 children under 5 are expected to suffer from acute malnutrition,' including 41,000 severe cases where children would be 'at heightened risk of death.'"

The IPC is expected to release a full report on conditions in Gaza "in the coming days." Prior to releasing the report, they have assessed that the Gaza Strip would be in Phase 2, the "alert" phase for malnutrition, between July and December 2026. They state that "74,200 children aged 6–59 months will likely require treatment for acute malnutrition through April 2027, with more than 11,400 severe cases expected."

UNICEF’s July report found that "very few confirmed nutrition-related deaths have been reported during treatment" in Gaza. The IPC did not respond to questions about UNICEF’s findings, or whether they stood by their prior claims that famine had been reached in Gaza.

HAMAS AGREES TO COMPLETE DISARMAMENT UNDER 'HISTORIC' GAZA AGREEMENT: TRUMP

WASHINGTON, DC - JULY 24: U.S. Rep. Rashida Tlaib (D-MI), joined by Palestinian rights activists, speaks at a press conference on food aid to Gaza, outside the U.S. Capitol on July 24, 2025 in Washington, DC. Tlaib spoke on the recent United Nation's report that noted over 1,000 Palestinians have been killed seeking aid since late May, hundreds of them at sites managed by the Israeli and US-backed Gaza Humanitarian Foundation. (Photo by Kevin Dietsch/Getty Images) (Kevin Dietsch/Getty Images)

The State Department spokesperson added that "the United States, in coordination with Israel, have facilitated humanitarian assistance while taking important steps to prevent Hamas from diverting or looting the aid, providing more support to Gazans. The President has a bold and ambitious plan to rebuild Gaza, which is well underway through the efforts of the Board of Peace to facilitate disarming Hamas and ensure it is no longer a threat to Israel."

Andrew Fox, a senior fellow at the Henry Jackson Society who has closely studied the Gaza conflict, told Fox News Digital that "the new data shows that the allegations of famine in Gaza were pure hysteria." He said that while "certain small pockets of hunger occurred in Gaza, we now know this can only have been an issue of distribution. Once again, international organizations removed Hamas and their share of the blame for Gaza’s suffering from the conversation, stoking the anti-Israel narrative."

Prof. Aron Troen, director of the Nutrition and Brain Health Laboratory and teaches in the School of Nutrition Science and the School of Public Health at The Hebrew University in Jerusalem, told Fox News Digital that the UNICEF findings are "very, very good news." He said it was "remarkable that in an area which was very recently claimed to be experiencing not only famine, but a deliberate and imposed political famine, that the situation has gone to the point that the current measures, and at least some of them, right now are better than…other places in the Arab world."

Palestinians carry aid supplies, that entered Gaza on trucks through Israel, in Beit Lahia, in the northern Gaza Strip July 29, 2025. (Ebrahim Hajjaj/Reuters)

CHRISTIAN LEADERS HOLD EMERGENCY SUMMIT IN JERUSALEM TO CONFRONT GLOBAL RISE IN ANTISEMITISM

"It’s important to state that if one wishes to take seriously the efforts to identify humanitarian need and provide an adequate response, then you have to be just as open to the good news as to the bad news," Troen said. He further decried "narratives" surrounding the report "that serve political agendas." He said that if there were the possibility of "a gradual transfer of pragmatic agency to a Palestinian governance in the interests of two states, respect for borders, coexistence," that it "requires people to stop throwing around genocide, famine, and impugning one side or the other in order to gain political leverage."

Kurtis Cooper, Chief of Global Media at UNICEF, told Fox News Digital that "the recent nutrition survey measures conditions in mid-2026, more than nine months after the IPC confirmed famine in August 2025 and after a ceasefire and substantial scale-up in humanitarian assistance. It does not tell us what conditions were in August 2025, and it was never designed to."

Geneva, Switzerland - September 3, 2020: Headquarters of the Regional Office for Europe and Central Asia of the UNICEF, a UN agency created in 1946 to improve children's condition worldwide. (iStock)

Cooper said that "in terms of why the situation has improved, during the period covered by the August 2025 IPC analysis, programmes to detect and treat malnutrition were largely operating, but blanket supplementary feeding had largely ceased across Gaza because of severe access constraints and supply disruptions. Programme data show a similar trend: admissions for treatment of acute malnutrition peaked at nearly 17,000 children in August 2025 before falling to around 3,100 by May 2026."

Cooper did not answer questions about how WHZ rates measured in Gaza compare to those in other countries experiencing widespread human suffering.

IDF forces are seen operating in Rafah, a city in the Gaza Strip. (IDF Spokesman's Unit)

In May, UNICEF reported that in Sudan, "almost 100,000 children were admitted for treatment for severe acute malnutrition" between January and March. UNICEF estimated that 825,000 children under five would experience severe acute malnutrition in Sudan in 2026.

Andrew Fox called on "leading organizations" to "offer a public and full retraction of their error-strewn papers." He explained that "their mistakes have paved the way for an explosion in global antisemitism, and these organizations must own their roles in that and make amends as loudly as possible."

According to the J7 Large Communities’ Task Force Against Antisemitism, 2025 was the deadliest year for antisemitic attacks around the world since 1994.

Beth Bailey writes on the United Nations, worldwide antisemitism, and regions in conflict for Fox News.

articles.title: Lottery ticket sold at Illinois gas station wins $1bn Powerball jackpot
articles.excerpt:
Prize was eighth largest in Powerball history and followed three months without a top prize winner

A Powerball ticket sold at a gas station in western Illinois was the sole winner of the $1bn jackpot...
articles.body_text:
Prize was eighth largest in Powerball history and followed three months without a top prize winner

A Powerball ticket sold at a gas station in western Illinois was the sole winner of the $1bn jackpot, ending a three-month drought without a top-prize victor.

The ticket that won the jackpot on Wednesday night was purchased at a Hy-Vee station in Quincy, about 100 miles (160km) west of the state capital of Springfield along the Missouri border, Illinois Lottery officials said. The winning numbers were 4-26-66-67-69 with the Powerball number of 9.

It was not immediately clear if the winner has come forward yet.

The prize comes in the form of either an annuity of $1bn paid over 29 years or a lump-sum payment of $450.5m. Winners almost always take the lump sum.

The $1.04bn grand prize was the eighth largest in Powerball history, game organizers said. Another lottery game, Mega Millions has also had a $1bn jackpot winner.

The record lottery jackpot still stands at just over $2bn, won with a Powerball ticket purchased in California in 2022.

articles.title: Piranha drama: boy, 8, hooks fearsome exotic fish in Pennsylvania lake
articles.excerpt:
South American fish with razor-toothed jaws was probably released by someone who owned it as a pet, officials say

An eight-year-old boy fishing for bass in Pennsylvania was stunned to catch something...
articles.body_text:
South American fish with razor-toothed jaws was probably released by someone who owned it as a pet, officials say

An eight-year-old boy fishing for bass in Pennsylvania was stunned to catch something more associated with the Amazon – and countless horror movies – than the rolling landscape of the eastern US.

Seamus Coffey, who was fishing with his father Michael in a lake near Philadelphia, hauled in a large red-bellied piranha, complete with the razor-toothed jaws that the fearsome breed is so famous for.

Michael Coffey recalled to ABC that he told his son “Slow down dude, you might lose it” as he pulled in the hefty catch that he could not recognise. But Sean quickly identified the species.

“He said, ‘It’s a piranha!’” Michael said and when asked how he knew, Seamus replied: “Because I watch YouTube!”

The Pennsylvania fish and boat commission later confirmed the identification.

“Our biologists have confirmed that this is some species of piranha,” said Mike Parker, a spokesperson for the agency, to ABC.

The broadcaster said that officials assumed the fish had made it into Pennsylvania’s waters because it had been released by someone who owned it as an exotic pet. Such actions can have a devastating impact in local wildlife.

“It’s a lifelong responsibility for many of these species that do live fairly long lives and are expensive to take care of, require a special habitat, special food, a lot of care,” Parker told ABC.

“And people quickly tire of that and decide the best thing to do for this animal would be to go throw it in the river, go throw it in a pond. That is probably the worst thing you can do for an animal that’s been a pet.”

The Coffeys did not release the piranha back into the lake and they disposed of it humanely.

articles.title: Italian businessman admits organising bombing at home of journalist and friend
articles.excerpt:
Valter Lavitola’s lawyer says he had intended attack to boost security for investigative reporter Sigfrido Ranucci

An Italian businessman has admitted to masterminding a bomb attack at the home of Si...
articles.body_text:
Valter Lavitola’s lawyer says he had intended attack to boost security for investigative reporter Sigfrido Ranucci

An Italian businessman has admitted to masterminding a bomb attack at the home of Sigfrido Ranucci, a prominent investigative journalist, claiming it was intended to boost his security protection.

Valter Lavitola, who was friends with Ranucci, the host of Report, an investigative programme aired by the state broadcaster, Rai, made the confession to investigators after his arrest earlier this week in connection with the case, the businessman’s lawyer, Sergio Cola, told the Italian media.

It was originally thought that the mafia had been behind the attack in October last year when a rudimentary but powerful bomb was detonated outside Ranucci’s home in a town near Rome, almost destroying his car and another owned by his daughter.

Four other people allegedly commissioned by Lavitola were arrested in late June on suspicion of carrying out the attack.

Cola said Lavitola had orchestrated the attack in order to boost Ranucci’s security detail amid threats to his life from the mafia.

“He did it for Ranucci’s good, because he was a target of attacks,” he said.

Lativola denied allegations that the motive had been to enhance Ranucci’s popularity with the aim of him entering politics, something Lativola allegedly hoped to benefit from too.

The allegations were outlined in an investigative report, seen by the Guardian, which included telephone conservations including one allegedly from Lavitola telling Ranucci “you will be prime minister in two years”.

There has been no suggestion from investigators that Ranucci, who previously expressed shock over Lavitola’s alleged involvement, was aware of the plot.

Ranucci, whose investigations for Report focus on alleged crime and corruption, often involving government ministers, is suing unnamed commentators and politicians who accused him of staging the attack for his own benefit for defamation.

His lawyer, Roberto De Vita, said that if the allegations of Lavitola’s motive were correct then Ranucci was “a victim three times over”.

“He is a victim of a serious, dangerous attack, of betrayal, of being exploited by a friend in a delirious show of madness and, last but not least – and perhaps most seriously – of a massive and persistent campaign of media and political lynching that, through conjecture and insinuations, has sought to portray the victim as the more-or-less-willing beneficiary of the attack.”

The case has unfolded amid a broader debate about press freedom in Italy and journalists’ safety.

Ranucci has been outspoken about the alleged interference in Rai by Giorgia Meloni’s far-right government. The broadcaster opened an internal audit into his journalistic methods after it emerged in early July that Lavitola was being interrogated in connection with the bomb attack. The deputy prime minister, Matteo Salvini, has called for him to be suspended.

There have been questions over Ranucci’s relationship with Lavitola, a former journalist who owns a restaurant in Rome. They became friends in 2019 after Ranucci conducted an investigation into Lavitola, who has been embroiled in several legal proceedings in the past, including one resulting in a conviction for extorting the late former prime minister Silvio Berlusconi.

Ranucci told Corriere della Sella in early July that he had “never hidden” the friendship, describing it as perhaps a case of “Stockholm syndrome”.

articles.title: College golfer delivers US Amateur upset with added pressure of having just one extra golf ball
articles.excerpt:
Dan Zaksheske, Zach Dean & Dan Dakich react to Charlie Woods snapping at a spectator for a camera noise during his back swing

Competing in the US Amateur, the most prestigious amateur golf tournament...
articles.body_text:
Dan Zaksheske, Zach Dean & Dan Dakich react to Charlie Woods snapping at a spectator for a camera noise during his back swing

Competing in the US Amateur, the most prestigious amateur golf tournament in the world, is already stressful enough. Showing up to the first tee to take on one of the top seeds in the field with just two golf balls to your name, well, that presents a whole new level of stress, and one that Ryder Cowan experienced at Merion Golf Club on Wednesday.

Cowan, a senior at Oklahoma, made his way through a 16-man playoff for 11 spots to earn the No. 59 seed in the 64-man match play bracket and drew junior phenom six-seed Miles Russell in his first match.

Despite entering the week ranked eighth in the World Amateur Golf Rankings (WAGR) fresh off of co-low amateur honors at the U.S. Open, Cowan was the underdog against Russell, who won't graduate high school until 2027.

Amateur Ryder Cowan of the United States lines up a putt on the 1st hole during the final round of the 126th U.S. OPEN at Shinnecock Hills Golf Club on June 21, 2026 in Southampton, New York. (Photo by David Cannon/Getty Images) (David Cannon/Getty Images)

TEENAGE GOLFER MILES RUSSELL DELIVERS HIS DAD AN ALL-TIME FATHER'S DAY EXPERIENCE DURING US OPEN FINAL ROUND

Russell is the top-ranked junior player in the world, ranked fourth in the WAGR, and has put together a junior career comparable to Tiger Woods.

Cowan was certainly aware of the situation, but it didn't allow it to phase him, at least not during his match against Russell. Prior to teeing off is a different story.

Ryder Cowan of the United States bounces a ball on his putter after finishing the 16th hole on day three of the U.S. Amateur Championship at Merion Golf Club on August 12, 2026 in Ardmore, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Isaiah Vazquez/Getty Images) (Isaiah Vazquez/Getty Images)

OUTKICK IS NOW ON THE FOX APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD

According to Golf Channel's Brentley Romine, Cowan forgot to bring sleeves of new golf balls to the course, leaving him with one new golf ball and one "fairly used" one in his golf bag. He stuck with the new golf ball for the first 10 holes of the match before swapping to the used one.

The used golf ball came with a bit of magic, too, with Cowan chipping in for par on the 17th hole to pull off the upset against Russell 2&1. The Sooner actually flubbed his first chip shot on the Par 3 before holing his next attempt with pristine touch.

When you're one of the top amateur golfers on the planet, the stresses of playing with just one spare golf ball are different than if a 15 handicap pulled the same move.

Ryder Cowan of the United States hits his second shot on the 10th hole on day two of the U.S. Amateur Championship at Merion Golf Club on August 11, 2026 in Ardmore, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Isaiah Vazquez/Getty Images) (Isaiah Vazquez/Getty Images)

Just like professional golfers do, Cowan likely switches to a new golf ball a handful of times over the course of 18 holes, especially if he is hitting a lot of full wedge shots, which can cause serious wear and tear. There is also, of course, the possibility of hitting a cart path or even a tree, which can damage a golf ball enough to virtually make it unplayable when we're talking about the highest level of amateur player.

As for the 15 handicap, their biggest fear would be losing both golf balls and having to embarrassingly ask their playing partner for a spare.
